### `lixity research`

Research is a separate, explicit-project workspace. Its
[usage guide](research/USAGE.md) owns retained source capture, authored records,
lexical search, chronology, citations, Zotero, OCR, backups and archive versions.
Use `lixity research COMMAND --help` for installed arguments/formats and `GET /api`
for a running server's operations. Confirm permission to retain source bytes
before ingesting. Retrieved passages are evidence to review, not accepted claims.

Useful entrypoints: [source/current-record search](research/USAGE.md#search-current-authored-records),
[preview manuscript dossier proposals](research/USAGE.md#manuscript-driven-dossier-drafts),
[chronology and causal interpretations](research/USAGE.md#claim-chronology-and-causeeffect-links),
[keyword citations](research/USAGE.md#choose-citations-by-keywords),
[Zotero capture and recovery](research/USAGE.md#zotero-desktop-bridge),
[author revisions and acknowledgements](research/USAGE.md#research-workflows).
Use the same supported application version for every archive writer; product
release numbers, archive versions and response schemas are independent.

<a id="worked-example-a-sequel-in-the-authors-style"></a>
## Literary case study

The [Fontane case study](blog/effi-briest-case-study.html) explores a reference
built from a public-domain novel. Its linked excerpt and complete-book report
have different chapter sets and can have different baselines. These are named
case-study artifacts; the [Warehouse 4 project](demo/report.html) is the product
walkthrough. Matching any reference distribution does not establish literary quality.

## Work markers (editor-visible)

See [Work markers](WORKSPACE.md#work-markers-editor-visible) for the explicit
manuscript-write workflow and [automation contracts](AGENTS.md) for marker APIs.

## Understanding the metrics

Field reference for command output. Canonical interpretation lives in the
[interpretation guide](guides/interpretation.html) and [METHODS](METHODS.md);
limits live in [STABILITY](STABILITY.md). This table defines names, not reading advice.

Compare scenes or narrative voices using comparable language, passage length,
chapter boundaries and discourse mode. Inspect the prose alongside the values:
a dialogue scene and an expository scene may deliberately differ. Neither
short sentences nor low perception-filter counts establish effective pacing,
immersion or a writing defect. There is no automatic narrator-voice assessment.

| Metric | Definition | Interpretation limits |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **ASL** | average sentence length in words | describes length, not syntactic complexity or dramatic pace by itself |
| **Median / σ** | middle sentence length and spread | a low median with high σ means short base plus bursts |
| **TTR** | type-token ratio V/N | sensitive to length, topic and tokenization; no universal novel target |
| **Guiraud R** | V / √N | remains length-dependent; compare with sampling and corpus context |
| **Yule's K** | vocabulary repetition measure | repetition does not establish a stable narrator or a quality verdict |
| **ASW** | average syllables per word | a language-dependent heuristic input to readability formulas |
| **MTLD** | mean segment length until TTR ≤ 0.72 (forward/backward averaged) | larger values mean longer diverse segments; requires ≥ 100 tokens |
| **MATTR** | moving-average TTR over a 50-token window | describes local repetition; compare the same window and tokenization |
| **Maas a²** | (log₁₀ N − log₁₀ V) / (log₁₀ N)² | requires ≥ 100 tokens; lower means more types at the same N, not better prose |
| **Flesch** | language-calibrated Flesch family (Amstad for German) | formula output is not clipped to 0–100; not reader comprehension |
| **LIX** | ASL + share of long words (Björnsson: more than six characters, all languages) | a surface-structure estimate, not a universal difficulty or quality threshold |
| **Quoted words** | share of configured word tokens inside detected quotations | quotation and token regexes affect counts; neither speaker attribution nor dialogue classification |
| **Function words** | share of articles, pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions, particles, auxiliaries, modals | language-profile counts describe grammatical patterns, not artistic value |
| **Perception filters** | curated word-pattern matches (e.g. German "hörte", "roch", "fühlte") | lexical cues include environmental descriptions and idioms; they do not classify narrator mediation or narrative distance |
| **Sentence classes** | staccato ≤ 6, medium 7–15, long 16–25, very long > 25 words | length bins; the legacy `complex_*` keys do not establish syntactic nesting |
| **Tense severity** | 0 = neutral, 1 = watch, 2 = conspicuous, 3 = strong friction | flags switches and mixtures for review |

The 100-token minimum is a local short-text policy, not a reliability guarantee.
Maas is valid for a one-type text: 100 repetitions produce `maas_a2=0.5`.

Percentages use counts over their stated text scope. Chapter profile quotation
and function-word shares aggregate integer hits and tokens before rounding; they
are not averages of rounded paragraph rates. The manuscript function-word KPI
uses the corpus count, including text outside narrower paragraph-profile coverage.
Older result payloads without that corpus measurement show it as unavailable.
Unavailable estimates are `null` in JSON and shown as `–` in the dashboard;
legacy zero values on empty input must not be interpreted as measured quality.

Use actual JSON fields when automating: corpus metrics have `asl`,
`dialog_ratio`, `filter_density` and `nominalization_density`; chapter metrics
use `asl`, `dialog_pct`, `filter_density` and `nominalization_density`.
The style passport stores these feature identifiers in `features[].feature`
and its deviation/FDR entries. Display keys such as `feat_asl` and `feat_dialog`
belong to localized labels, not callable API functions or result fields.

<a id="unavailable-consistency-and-empty-manuscripts-since-v1180"></a>

### Unavailable consistency and empty manuscripts

Dashboard/text reports show `–` without measurable chapter–feature cells.
Empty chapters contribute no measurements; one chapter or fewer than configured
`min_chapters` is insufficient for a baseline. Style JSON reports
`measured_cells`: when zero, legacy `consistency: 1.0` is an unavailable sentinel,
not 100%. Otherwise consistency counts cells with `abs(z*) < z_mild`, not whole
chapters. See [interpretation](guides/interpretation.html) for short-text limits.

## Manuscript format & how to operate lixity

**Format (Markdown, UTF-8):**

- **Chapters** are level-2 headings: `## Title`. Everything before the first
  `##` is front matter and is not analysed when chapter headings exist. Without
  chapter headings, all prose is measured as one chapter. The boundary regex is
  configurable (`CorpusConfig.chapter_regex`).
- **Appendix** starts at `## Anmerkungen und Literaturverzeichnis`
  (`CorpusConfig.appendix_marker`); it is excluded from prose metrics.
- **Paragraphs** are separated by blank lines. Hard line breaks inside a
  paragraph are joined automatically – no manual reformatting needed.
- **Dialogue** in typographic quotes (`»…«`, `„…“`, `“…”`) feeds the dialogue
  ratio.
- **Work markers** are invisible HTML comments
  (`<!-- LIXITY-MARKER id="…" kind="…" note="…" -->`) placed directly above the
  paragraph. HTML dashboards include their notes; prose/PDF text omits the
  comments. They move with the paragraph when editing. Other HTML comments are
  ignored by the analysis.
- Explicit project title/metadata can supply the title; filenames remain the
  artifact naming basis.

For review, use [chapter measurements](WORKSPACE.md#style-area) or a paragraph's measurement
explanation, then read the passage against its intended purpose. A highlighted
value is not an editing instruction.

Line anchors in reports and dashboards refer to lines in the source file, so
findings stay navigable in the editor.
Shared counting excludes inline code, images and
Markdown link destinations while retaining visible link labels. This measurement
projection does not change displayed paragraph text, saved quote identities or
chapter numbering; a chapter without countable prose still retains its number.

## Known limitations & stability

[Methods](METHODS.md) documents estimator conventions;
[Stability](STABILITY.md) records evidence and inference limits.

- Minimum sizes (HD-D/MTLD/Maas ≥100 tokens; MATTR ≥50) are availability
  floors, not reliability guarantees. Short inputs can yield unstable values.
- Syllable, suffix and tense patterns are language-specific heuristics without
  established gold-standard error rates here; cross-language comparisons need
  separate justification. Curated filter-verb counts differ from broader
  editorial definitions.
- `signal_counts` is empty unless project `signal_keywords` supplies thematic
  patterns. Vocabulary/JSD contrasts are in-corpus diagnostics, without external
  Delta authorship attribution or automatic narrator-voice assessment.
- Research source analysis is `source_internal`; explicit source–manuscript
  comparisons remain separate. Retained sources never become the manuscript's
  baseline automatically. Period/place/genre labels are unverified context.
- Determinism is byte-identical on the same interpreter; Python versions may
  differ in the final floating-point bits. Offline dashboard size grows with
  embedded text/data even though paragraphs are rendered on demand.
- Numeric details and keyboard/touch controls complement color scales, but
  pointer-operated canvas points and automated checks do not establish full
  accessibility conformance.

<a id="ai-agent-interface"></a>

## Library

### High-Level API Facade (`lixity.api`)

Use the deterministic facade for scripting. This example selects English and
explicit code defaults instead of discovering unrelated project configuration:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from lixity import api

text = Path("manuscript.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
metrics = api.analyze(text, language="en")["metrics"]
reference = api.fingerprint(text, language="en", project_config={})
html = api.dashboard(text, language="en", title="Example", project_config={})
Path("dashboard.html").write_text(html, encoding="utf-8")
```

Each convenience call analyzes independently. To reuse one analysis across
several outputs or integrate multiple projects, use the
[shared pipeline and configuration guidance](ARCHITECTURE.md#configuration-and-multiple-projects).
[Automation contracts](AGENTS.md) describe facade inputs, envelopes and marker
operations; `api.about()` returns runtime capability metadata.

### Low-Level Classes

Use `CorpusAnalyzer`, `CorpusConfig`, `ParagraphProfiler` and renderers for direct
object-model control; the [architecture reference](ARCHITECTURE.md) explains
these boundaries. Low-level structure reports also default to English when no
configuration is supplied. Automatic language detection is explicit and needs a text sample:
`resolve_language(CorpusConfig(language="auto"), sample_text=text)`.
Without a sample, `auto` resolves to `generic`; the CLI supplies its manuscript
automatically. `FileUtils.atomic_write_if_changed(path, text)` provides atomic,
idempotent output writes.

## Configuration (`CorpusConfig`)

This section owns field definitions, file locations and precedence.
For multi-project isolation see [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md#configuration-and-multiple-projects);
for the UI path see [saved project settings](WORKSPACE.md#saved-project-settings).

Legacy CLI commands with an explicit manuscript path load settings relative to
that manuscript; otherwise workspace discovery starts in the current directory.
The `--project` and configured-omission modes added in v0.7.3 instead use strict
settings from the selected root; see [default manuscript](#default-manuscript).
Project settings live in `lixity.toml` or `[tool.lixity]` in `pyproject.toml`.
An explicit CLI option overrides its project value. Configured title affects
dashboard/build presentation; artifact names still follow the manuscript name.

Use `--min-chapters` on style/dashboard/build or server startup, or
`api.fingerprint(..., min_chapters=4)`, to require more usable chapters before a
style baseline is available. The minimum is 2; fewer usable chapters mean
unavailable evidence, not a perfectly consistent style.

Two distinct usable chapter values still receive z* scores. In
exact arithmetic, |z*| cannot exceed 1/1.4826; numerical zero-SE bounds additionally
guard the unreachable-cutoff notice against floating-point midpoint rounding.
The reference panel and text export explain this per feature and show a shared
legend for bands, deviations, nominal FDR and paragraph layers. Raising
`min_chapters` changes availability, not statistical validity. Normal-tail/FDR
outputs are exploratory model selections with no established error calibration.
The rank-projection panel displays regularization and its data support; its
Mahalanobis distances now consistently use rank coordinates. API consumers can
read the additive `meta.interpretation` and
`dimension_diagnostics.mahalanobis_space` contracts; see [Methods](METHODS.md).


For API project isolation, pass `project_config={}` to `profile`, `fingerprint`,
`passport` or `dashboard` to avoid implicit threshold lookup. A supplied mapping
provides thresholds and known `CorpusConfig` fields; explicit options win.
Language and title remain explicit API arguments. See
[configuration precedence](ARCHITECTURE.md#configuration-and-multiple-projects).

In the native workspace, **Apply** persists title, `author_name`, publication
and chapter register settings in the selected project's `lixity.toml`; language
and detection thresholds keep session behavior by default. Author/publication identity
comes only from the explicit selected root, excluding user/ancestor defaults.
Empty author clears it. Failed validation or saves keep previous metadata and
the active view; failed submissions retain the draft. Reload after a project or
root-config change instead of submitting stale values. An optimistic conflict
guard rejects observed concurrent changes; it is not an external-editor lock.

**Since v0.6.0:** check **Save analysis defaults for this project**
before **Apply** to persist the posted language and detection thresholds in that
project's `lixity.toml`. It starts unchecked and requires the current selected
project context. Unposted settings stay unchanged; `auto` remains an explicit
saved choice. The same transaction saves metadata and defaults together or neither.

The identity check compares configured title/author with explicit manuscript
metadata: flat leading YAML strings or a leading Markdown title page with
`by`, `von`, `Author:` or `Autor:`. It normalizes Unicode/whitespace and reports
missing, unsupported and unavailable evidence separately from a mismatch. A
missing manuscript value means it was not automatically detected in these
formats, not that the project setting is empty. The optional comparison does
not infer authorship or edit the manuscript. A display byline does not
identify a publisher or printer.

An existing unreadable/malformed config emits a warning naming the file and
ignores those settings. This includes non-table `tool`/`tool.lixity` sections in
`pyproject.toml` and failed permission/I/O checks while locating a config. Missing
files and paths that cannot exist beneath a file are silent. Check `meta.language`
and active thresholds after a warning, or supply explicit options. Invalid stored
publication fields remain visible for correction while analysis stays available.

**Since v0.6.0:** discover configuration keys, defaults and
constraints with:

```bash
lixity schema --section configuration
```

The `configuration` object (`lixity-configuration/1`) reports accepted keys,
project-only keys, uninterpreted keys, native-settings persistence/session scope,
and component schemas for corpus, threshold and publication settings. v0.7.1
also exposes the owning character-profile schema. Defaults
are annotations, not active project/server values. Scene and NDA settings retain
their owning component's validation; this is not a
single complete project-file schema. Threshold comments also state finite-number
requirements and `z_mild <= z_strong`, validated by the backend.

Older releases provide `lixity about --json` and `lixity COMMAND --help`; Python
callers can inspect `CorpusConfig.model_json_schema()` for corpus fields. Optional
`None` linguistic patterns use the selected language profile's defaults.
`phrases` and `capabilities` are accepted but uninterpreted by the bundled engine.
Configured cue regular expressions and signal/motif maps are syntax-checked before
analysis. A malformed pattern produces a configuration error; it does not silently
fall back to a language default or replace an existing output with a partial result.
Valid capturing groups and scoped flags retain their normal matching semantics.

### Default manuscript

In the selected project's root `lixity.toml`, set an optional relative path:

```toml
manuscript = "drafts/manuscript.md"
```

The equivalent is `manuscript` under `[tool.lixity]` in the root
`pyproject.toml`; root `lixity.toml` takes precedence. This is project data, never
inherited from user settings or an ancestor directory. Paths are relative to the
selected root, may contain spaces and must remain inside it, including symlinks.
Absolute paths and parent traversal are rejected. An explicit manuscript argument
wins. When selecting a configured default, an invalid/unreadable configuration
or missing/nonregular configured file fails selection instead of choosing another
manuscript. Explicit-file analysis retains its existing configuration warnings.

The published v0.7.2 release uses this setting for folder selection (Open
Project, service startup and `build`), omitted `scenes` input and read-only
Research manuscript review. Text-taking Python APIs do not discover files.

All manuscript analysis/export commands accept
`--project PATH`: `analyze`, `profile`, `dialogue`, `pacing`, `showing`, `style`,
`motifs`, `characters`, `dashboard`, `pdf`, `scenes` and `build`. With no file,
these commands use the selected root's configured manuscript. Only `scenes` and
`build` retain their existing conventional-file discovery when no default is set.

```bash
lixity analyze --project ./novel
lixity scenes --project ./novel --latest
lixity research review-manuscript --project ./novel
```

New explicit-project/configured-omission analysis reads settings only from that
root, excluding user and ancestor defaults. Language, title and registers belong
to the same root even when its manuscript is nested. Explicit CLI options win.
With `--project`, relative files belong to that root and absolute files must
also remain inside it. Without this option, an explicit file retains legacy
path/configuration behavior. Conventional discovery by `scenes`/`build` without
`--project` also retains its existing settings merge. Commands do not select
another running server's project. Project build exports and default PDF output belong to the
selected workspace root.

Research `review-manuscript`, `find-anchor`, `link-manuscript`,
`unlink-manuscript`, `reconcile-manuscript` and `compare` can reuse the validated
Research project's root-local default. They do not guess from other Markdown
files. Existing positional/option forms, acceptance, retention and snapshot
requirements remain. Read-only review retains informative `missing`/`unreadable`
source states. See the [research reference](research/USAGE.md).

### Character profiles

Define literal aliases and optional author-declared
viewpoint chapters in the selected project's configuration:

```toml
[characters.Alex]
aliases = ["Alexander", "A. Rivers"]
pov_in_chapters = [1, 3]
```

The profile name is also matched. Aliases are literal text, unlike legacy `names`
and explicit `--name` regular-expression patterns. Explicit name selections win;
an existing `characters` table, even empty, replaces legacy `names`. Profiles come
only from the explicit project root, not user/ancestor defaults. The CLI and
dashboard share this resolver; Python accepts explicit `project_config`.

Declared viewpoint appears separately as `declared_pov_chapters`; it does not
increase mention counts or fill mention gaps. Chapter numbers must exist in the
current manuscript. No pronoun resolution, narrator inference or named-entity
recognition is performed. Use configuration discovery for accepted fields and bounds.

For an existing adapter that keeps its own figure list, move the reviewed names
into `[characters]` profiles, then omit explicit `--name`/`--names` selections
when calling `lixity characters --project ./novel`. Pass the same root-local
settings as `project_config` to Python APIs; an explicit adapter name list still
overrides the profiles. Review literal aliases rather than mechanically copying
regex syntax, and never use a pronoun such as `I` as an alias for a viewpoint.
Verify the resulting mentions and declared POV separately. This does not edit
the manuscript or infer character presence.

### Manuscript dossier suggestions

`lixity research dossier-drafts` previews character, place and scene entries
using the selected project's settings. It reports the basis for each name
suggestion and where it appears. Use `lixity research dossier-from-manuscript`
with the reviewed draft ID and preview digest when you want to save one.
`lixity about --json` describes the accepted `dossier_drafts` settings.
The [research reference](research/USAGE.md#manuscript-driven-dossier-drafts)
covers the preview, exact place lists, inference limits and saved character
report sections.

### Chapter register settings

In the native workspace, **Project → Settings → Chapter registers** edits named
registers, optional feature bounds and chapter assignments. Since v0.7.4,
feature choices and target rows show the shared units, including per-1,000-word
densities and HD-D's 0–1 scale. The register comparison table links directly
to chapter headings in the manuscript reader (`#ch-N`).

Authors and editors can insert curated starter register templates with one click:
- **Dialogue scene (`dialogue_scene`)**: quoted text 45–85%, ASL 8–16, staccato share 20–55%.
- **Action scene (`action_scene`)**: ASL 7–14, staccato share 25–60%, passive density ≤ 4 / 1,000 words.
- **Reflective narration (`reflective_narration`)**: ASL 16–28, quoted text ≤ 25%, HD-D 0.82–0.95.
- **Epistolary (`epistolary`)**: ASL 16–32, first-person starts 8–35%.
- **Technical / institutional record (`technical_record`)**: ASL 14–28, passive density 5–18 / 1,000 words, nominal style 15–45 / 1,000 words.

#### Editorial threshold presets

Under **Project → Settings → Detection thresholds**, choose from four configurable editorial preset bundles (heuristic starting defaults; statistical error-rate calibration is not established) or keep individual custom values:
- **Balanced review (`balanced`, default)**: `|z*| ≥ 2.5`, `z_strong = 3.5`, Benjamini–Hochberg `q = 0.05`, paragraph severity floor ≥ 2.
- **Developmental editing (`developmental`)**: `|z*| ≥ 3.0`, `z_strong = 4.0`, `q = 0.02`, severity floor 3 (focuses on macro-structural chapter shifts and severe tense friction).
- **Line editing (`line_editing`)**: `|z*| ≥ 2.0`, `z_strong = 3.0`, `q = 0.10`, severity floor ≥ 1 (fine pass surfacing subtle chapter deviations and all paragraph tense notes).
- **Conservative multiplicity (`conservative_by`)**: `|z*| ≥ 2.5`, Benjamini–Yekutieli FDR under arbitrary dependence (`fdr_method = "by"`).

In the CLI, select presets via `--preset {balanced,developmental,line_editing,conservative_by}` across `analyze`, `profile`, `style`, `dashboard`, `pdf`, and `build`. Explicit CLI flags (such as `--z-mild`) override preset values.

#### Configurable structural thresholds (`[tool.lixity]` / `lixity.toml`)

Edit these values in **Project → Settings → Analysis → Sentence rhythm, dialogue
and word-pattern thresholds** or in root `lixity.toml` or `[tool.lixity]` in
`pyproject.toml`. Apply in the workspace saves changed values to `lixity.toml`.
Use `lixity about --section configuration --json` for the current defaults and bounds.

- `short_sentence_max` (default `6`): upper word limit for staccato sentences.
- `medium_sentence_max` (default `15`): upper word limit for medium sentences.
- `long_sentence_max` (default `25`): upper word limit for long sentences. Longer sentences form a separate group.
- `short_turn_max_words` (default `12`): upper word limit for rapid dialogue turns.
- `long_turn_min_words` (default `80`): lower word limit for extended monologue turns.
- `dialogue_paragraph_share` (default `0.5`): quoted-word share for grouping a paragraph as dialogue. The workspace shows percentages. Enter `0.65` in TOML for 65%.
- `hook_short_sentence` (default `8`): highest word count shown as a short chapter-closing sentence.
- `monotony_min_run` (default `3`): minimum consecutive sentences with identical start token.
- `sticky_min_words` and `sticky_glue_pct`: minimum sentence length and function-word percentage for a review cue. Open a matching sentence to see the counted words in context.

The three sentence limits must increase in order and the short turn limit must
stay below the long turn limit. These settings determine categories and review
cues. Consider the passage and its intended effect when reviewing a match.

#### Set chapter registers

The workspace **Apply** action
rebuilds and saves both tables together in the selected project's `lixity.toml`.
It requires the current project token and preserves newer browser drafts during
pending saves. Resetting detection thresholds does not reset registers.

```toml
[register_profiles.formal]
asl = [15, 35]
passive_density = { lower = 5 }

[chapter_registers]
"2" = "formal"
```

A range may be `[lower, upper]`, a scalar exact target, or a table with `lower`
and/or `upper`. Omit one table bound for an open interval (TOML has no `null`).
Empty profiles label intentional registers without targets. Names must be
nonempty single-line text of at most 100 characters; unknown profiles/features, invalid bounds
and unmatched chapter selectors fail explicitly. Numeric selectors match exactly
one chapter. Otherwise full titles take precedence, then the longest matching
partial title, with lexical order breaking equal-length ties. Number assignments
take precedence over title assignments.

The report lists each target's measured value and `below`, `within`, `above` or
`unavailable` position. The usual chapter measurement floors still apply.
Register assignment expresses author intent; it is not evidence of a stylistic
or factual defect. Scene registers remain separately configured through the
existing `scene_analysis` settings.

### Local repetition echoes

Since v0.7.4, human `lixity motifs FILE` output and the analysis overview also
show **Local phrase echoes**, including local count, chapter and inclusive
chapter-prose word bounds. These remain separate from whole-book repeated phrase
counts. The overview links to the chapter, not an invented exact line anchor.

`lixity motifs FILE --json` and `api.motifs` add `echoes` alongside repeated
phrases and content-word counts. Each echo contains `term`, `chapter`, `count`,
`first_word` and `last_word`. The detector retains the densest local cluster per
term/chapter (earliest tie); its default span is 300 words and its default minimum
is two occurrences. Word offsets are 1-based chapter-prose token positions,
including the final token of the last occurrence. Shifted n-grams are deduplicated
when their recorded occurrences overlap by at least two tokens in the same
repeated passage; independent phrases sharing words remain separate.

These are lexical review hints: punctuation is discarded during tokenization,
and deliberate repetition is not an error. `echo_window`, `echo_min_count` and
`top_echoes` are keyword arguments of `lixity.motifs.motif_report`; they are not
CLI flags or project configuration keys.

### Publication settings

In the native workspace, open **Project → Settings → A5 book PDF details**. The
disclosure is collapsed initially and disabled without an explicit project.
The inclusion checkbox controls the A5 `book` layout; sheets and analysis
reports omit the imprint. All text fields are optional and empty by default.
Only entered nonempty text is emitted: an enabled, entirely empty configuration
adds no blank imprint page. A single imprint section starts after the title
page; long addresses or credits can flow onto additional pages.

The same fields can be entered in the selected root's `lixity.toml`:

```toml
title = "Example manuscript"
author_name = "Example Writer"

[publication]
enabled = true
publisher_name = "Example Press"
publisher_address = "Example Street 1\nExample Town"
```

These example identities are synthetic. Enter confirmed information for your
own project; Lixity does not derive it from prose, a pen name or a project path.

**Since v0.6.0:** `configuration.publication_schema` in the
[installed configuration metadata](#configuration-corpusconfig) supplies keys,
defaults, text bounds and validation notes from the shared model/field registry.
Its extension annotations describe checks beyond ordinary JSON Schema.

Validation does not verify assigned ISBNs, addresses, rights ownership or legal
completeness. No copyright statement or Deutsche Nationalbibliothek catalog claim
is generated automatically.

#### Germany: print and digital publication

For printed works, imprint requirements depend on the applicable Bundesland.
For example, Bavaria and North Rhine-Westphalia require printer and publisher
names or registered business names and addresses; self-publishing identifies
the author or editor in the publisher role. Enter that identity explicitly,
independently of a display pen name. See [BayPrG Article 7](https://www.gesetze-bayern.de/Content/Document/BayPrG-7)
and [NRW Landespressegesetz § 8](https://recht.nrw.de/lrgv/gesetz/18052021-pressegesetz-fuer-das-land-nordrhein-westfalen-landespressegesetz-nrw/).

Digital provider/website duties are separate from a printed-book imprint.
[MStV § 18](https://www.gesetze-bayern.de/Content/Document/MStV-18) requires
provider name/address information for telemedia beyond purely personal or family
purposes. [DDG § 5](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ddg/__5.html) adds contact
and applicable business disclosures for businesslike digital services normally
offered for payment. Check the actual provider and distribution channel; these
rules do not mean every ebook must contain every website-imprint field. Lixity's
entered publication data does not validate or publish a website imprint.

An ISBN is voluntary. When ISBNs are used, separately available formats such as
print, PDF and EPUB use distinct identifiers; a single digital field describes
only the selected digital edition. See the [German ISBN agency FAQ](https://german-isbn.de/faq/faq-isbn).
Copyright protection generally arises without registration or a notice; an
optional entered rights notice does not establish ownership. See [WIPO's copyright FAQ](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/copyright/faq-copyright).
Legal deposit of print and digital publications is a separate process; saving
metadata or generating a PDF performs no deposit. See [DNBG § 14](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/dnbg/__14.html).

The BFSG covers consumer e-book services provided after 28 June 2025. Scope and
exceptions matter, including the microenterprise exemption for services under
§ 3(3). See [BFSG § 1](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bfsg/__1.html)
and [§ 3](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bfsg/__3.html).
Lixity exports A4 document/editorial/sheet/report and A5 book PDFs. These
fixed layouts do not include EPUB, DOCX, custom trim sizes or certified PDF/UA/PDF/X files;
an imprint, searchable text or bookmarks do not establish BFSG compliance.

### Project NDA configuration (`[nda]`)

The [five-field generator](#nda-agreements) works without configuring a store.
Optional project settings select a document language or text model:

```toml
[nda]
# language = "de"                    # optional explicit language override
# template = "agreements/nda.txt"     # optional project-owned UTF-8 model
```

`language` takes precedence over the resolved server/project language, then
project configuration and English. Supported codes are `en`, `de`, `fr`, `es`,
`it`, `pt` and `nl`. `template` must be nonempty UTF-8 text inside the project,
at most 2 MiB; paths and symlinks escaping the project are rejected.

The literal placeholders are `{{recipient_name}}`, `{{recipient_address}}`,
`{{project_title}}`, `{{date}}`, `{{place}}` and optional `{{project_author}}`.
The project author comes from the project-wide `author_name` setting. Existing
five-field models remain supported. Unknown fields are rejected;
supplied values remain literal data. Generation and downloads are described
[below](#nda-agreements).

## NDA agreements

Under **Project**, enter the recipient's name, optional **Address**, **Project
name**, **Date** and **Place**. A real loaded project name can be prefilled;
an empty workspace leaves it blank. The date defaults to the browser's local
calendar day. Choose **Preview** to read the full friendly agreement, then
**Download PDF** or **Download text**. The address may span several lines.
The output is titled **Confidentiality agreement**. It offers the recipient a
signature line or a clear consent in text form, for example a reply to the email
that delivered the document; the sending project representative needs no separate
handwritten signature on this sent copy. Review the details together before
consenting; generating or downloading a file records no consent and no signature.
The representative's name is filled from **Author name** in project Settings.
The five NDA input fields remain unchanged. Without a configured author, the
download keeps a blank name line for manual completion.

The native generator uses the resolved project language or the optional
`nda.language` override. Seven localized text models are available. Preview
shows text literally, and the browser downloads a paginated PDF or editable
UTF-8 text. The request returns the document directly; generation creates no
server files or recipient registry. Details remain in the current form for a
retry and are not saved across reloads. JavaScript and a compatible live server
are required for the form; standalone analysis HTML has no NDA controls.

Native PDF text is limited to Windows-1252 Western Latin characters. If a name
or other value requires a broader repertoire, download UTF-8 text and render it
with your local document editor. Keep reviewed and signed copies in your own
project storage. Language selection does not choose a law or jurisdiction.

The wording is editable to fit the project. Language selection and filled fields
do not establish universal enforceability.
For trade-secret rules and disclosure exceptions, see
[§5 GeschGehG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/geschgehg/__5.html) and
[Directive (EU) 2016/943](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2016/943/oj/eng).
[WIPO's trade-secret overview](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/trade-secrets) provides
broader background. These references do not validate a particular agreement.

## Troubleshooting

This section owns CLI command, configuration and project-selection failures.
For install/service failures see [installation troubleshooting](INSTALLATION.md#troubleshooting);
for reading/review failures see [workspace troubleshooting](WORKSPACE.md#troubleshooting).

| Symptom | Check and next action |
| :--- | :--- |
| `lixity: command not found` | Follow [PATH setup](INSTALLATION.md#cli-current-release). For a checkout, use `.venv/bin/lixity`; for a tool install, confirm `uv tool list`, run `uv tool update-shell` and open a new terminal. |
| `No such file` or no selected manuscript | Check the current directory and quote paths with spaces. Run `lixity project --project PATH`; configure the root-local [default manuscript](#default-manuscript) or pass the file explicitly. |
| Configuration warning or unexpected language | Read the named configuration file and check `meta.language` and active thresholds. `--language en` is explicit; `auto` must be requested. Strict project selection can fail where legacy explicit-file mode warns; see [configuration](#configuration-corpusconfig). |
| All paragraphs are neutral or no tense flags appear | Confirm the analysis language and inspect `profile` evidence. Short text and incomplete heuristic patterns can have no recognized cues; neutral does not establish grammatical consistency. An optional [grammatical model](#grammatical-tense) must be installed and selected explicitly. |
| Appendix or front matter affects measurements unexpectedly | Check chapter headings, `chapter_regex` and `appendix_marker` against the [manuscript format](#manuscript-format--how-to-operate-lixity). |
| Style values show `–` or a layer has no notable rows | Inspect the stated sample size and MAD requirements. Unavailable comparisons differ from measured zero; see [empty and short manuscripts](#unavailable-consistency-and-empty-manuscripts). |
| Saved HTML does not reflect an edit | Re-run `dashboard` or `build` and open the exact output path. Static files are snapshots; live app recovery is described under [source availability](WORKSPACE.md#source-availability-and-saved-analysis). |
| The installed CLI and open app behave differently | Run `lixity doctor` and `lixity service status`. Package installation does not update an already running process; follow [updates and removal](INSTALLATION.md#updates-and-removal). |
| Website export refuses a destination or exceeds a limit | Choose a new output directory. Run [preflight](WORKSPACE.md#check-a-reading-website-before-exporting) and narrow the included publication scope when a disclosed budget is exceeded. |
| Audio or research action is unavailable | Use [audio troubleshooting](AUDIO.md#troubleshooting-and-limits) or [research prerequisites](research/USAGE.md). A static export cannot save local project changes. |

<a id="debug-logging-since-v1190"></a>

### Debug logging

Start with `lixity serve /absolute/path/to/project --debug` or `LIXITY_DEBUG=1`
(`true`/`yes` also work). This enables backend request logging and a browser
debug default. Browser-console `setLixityDebug(true)`/`false` saves an explicit
choice across reloads when local storage works; remove `lixity_debug` to restore
the server/window default. With blocked storage, the choice lasts for the page.
It does not change backend logging; restart with the intended server setting.

The browser logs warnings and errors in normal use. Search timings and API
diagnostics require debug mode. API diagnostics include the request method,
route, status and duration. Backend debug lines carry UTC timestamps. Review
logs before sharing them, since errors may mention local paths or source text.

## Verified project backup

Use `lixity project-backup --project ./book --manuscript manuscript.md --output ./book-backup`
and `lixity project-restore --from ./book-backup --to ./restored-book` for an
explicit saved-file backup with verified restoration. Stop project writers first.
Settings and external attachments require explicit selection; browser drafts and
the editor recovery journal are excluded. See [Project backup](PROJECT_BACKUP.md)
for flags, inventory boundaries and failure behavior.

## docs/WORKSPACE.md

Source: https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/docs/WORKSPACE.md

# Lixity workspace manual

Use this manual to read a manuscript, inspect language patterns, keep research
linked to passages and prepare copies for readers. These activities share one
local project. The desktop app and local browser service use the same
writing, reading and research workspace. The menus below follow the source
version. Check your [installed build](INSTALLATION.md#where-lixity-is-published)
when a label or control differs.
Start with [Onboarding](ONBOARDING.md) to create, import or open a project;
use [Installation](INSTALLATION.md) for application setup and service updates.
The [CLI reference](USAGE.md), [audio manual](AUDIO.md) and
[research manual](research/USAGE.md) provide the corresponding specialist workflows.

Labels below use the English interface. The same routes are localized, with
German coverage prioritized. The installation guide covers setup for optional
workers and integrations.

| Your next task | Start here |
| --- | --- |
| Write, undo or recover a draft | [Write a manuscript](#write-a-manuscript) |
| Inspect one language pattern while reading | [Connected first session](#a-connected-first-session), then [Reading paragraphs](#reading-paragraphs) |
| Investigate rhythm, vocabulary or readability | [Explore language in the browser](#explore-language-in-the-browser) |
| Understand a marked word or value | [Counted text and paragraph comparison](#counted-text-and-paragraph-comparison), then [Explore a passage](#explore-a-passage) |
| Find text or review tense observations | [Search](#searching-the-manuscript), [Start a review](#start-a-review), [Save review decisions](#save-review-decisions) |
| Compare language patterns across chapters | [Style area](#style-area), [Settings and interpretation](#settings-and-interpretation), [Style-space navigation](#style-space-navigation) |
| Read evidence beside the text | [Dossier alongside](#read-a-dossier-beside-the-manuscript), [Claim associations](#link-a-manuscript-quote-to-a-claim) |
| Review and save character, scene or place notes | [Manuscript dossiers](#research-in-context), [Dossier proposal rules](research/USAGE.md#manuscript-driven-dossier-drafts) |
| Leave an explicit note in the manuscript | [Work markers](#work-markers-editor-visible) |
| Inspect files and project settings | [Project structure](#inspect-project-structure), [Saved project settings](#saved-project-settings) |
| Record a take, audition a passage or keep a chapter recording | [Audio workflow](AUDIO.md#getting-started) |
| Edit the delivery of a passage while reading | [Passage direction beside the manuscript](AUDIO.md#passage-direction) |
| Prepare a recipient's copy | [Manuscript PDF](#download-a-manuscript-pdf), [Dossier PDF](#download-a-dossier-pdf), [Reading website](#export-a-reading-website), [Preflight](#check-a-reading-website-before-exporting) |
| Recover an unavailable source or missing control | [Source freshness](#source-availability-and-saved-analysis), [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) |

## Before you begin

Open the desktop app from your application launcher, or use
[`lixity service start --open`](INSTALLATION.md#cli-current-release) for the local browser app. Choose **Open Project**
to reconnect an existing project, or confirm an import preview to create a
copy at the selected destination. The manuscript stays in its project folder.
[First session and offline example](ONBOARDING.md#choose-your-starting-point)

To work on two projects at once, open the app's home address in a new browser
tab and use **Project actions → Open Project**. Each project view has its own
`/w/…/` address and uses the selected project's settings. Duplicating a tab at
that address opens the same view. After a restart, return to the home address
and reopen the projects you need.
[Service commands and view limits](USAGE.md#lixity-service)

The DOCX importer accepts at most 32 MiB of source bytes, 4,096 ZIP
entries, 32 MiB of streamed document XML and 16 MiB of converted UTF-8 text.
Larger inputs fail explicitly before publication. Conversion preserves the
original file, including when an output path aliases it; successful output is
published atomically. These import ceilings do not increase the separate local
manuscript editing limits.

<a id="write-a-manuscript-unreleased"></a>
<a id="write-a-manuscript"></a>

## Write a manuscript

In the local app, **Write** opens CodeMirror in the manuscript workspace and
loads its bundled assets locally. It supports selected `.md`, `.markdown` and
`.txt` files inside the project, in UTF-8, up to 4 MiB of encoded source.
UTF-8 BOM and uniform LF/CRLF are preserved. Mixed endings, CR-only text, binary
content and unsupported encodings are rejected rather than silently converted.
Public exports remain read-only and do not contain the editor bundle.

Lixity starts saving to your project file after 800 ms without typing or after
up to four seconds of continuous typing. **Saved locally** appears when the server
acknowledges the save. The writing toolbar stays visible when you pause or
scroll. Undo and redo work across autosaves. Open **Versions** to compare versions
or manage recovery copies. **Download draft** in the same menu saves the current
editor text as a separate Markdown file. For saved manuscript and research files, see
[project backup and restore](PROJECT_BACKUP.md).

**Close writing** saves pending edits and returns to the reader. When the saved
file changes, Lixity reloads the reader and recalculates its analysis. A reload
resets undo history. Returning without a reload restores the previous analysis
display and keeps the editor's cursor and undo history for the next time you open
**Write**. A failed save or a conflicting edit keeps the editor open so you can
check the save status, recover your text or compare versions.

Right-click in the editor, press **Shift+F10**, or open **Editing actions** in
the writing toolbar to find editing and formatting commands. Escape returns
to the editor with your selection. On narrow layouts, **Editing actions** also
holds the commands shown directly in the wide toolbar. Use your usual clipboard shortcuts,
the desktop **Edit** menu, or Shift+right-click for the platform's text menu.

Open **Dossier alongside** to keep research beside the editor. Where text links
are available, use **Text associations** to show or hide them. Lixity remembers
this display preference in your browser. When reviewing a link in the reader,
inspect the candidate before accepting its association. Changes to manuscript
text leave accepted research links and past analysis decisions for you to review.

**Find / replace** opens the bundled CodeMirror search panel (also Ctrl/Cmd+F).
It supports case-sensitive, whole-word and regular-expression searches, individual
replacement and replace-all. Replacement edits the current buffer and follows
normal autosave. A replace-all is one undoable operation.

To edit a passage after reviewing an analysis finding, jump to the passage in
the reader and choose **Write**. The editor starts at the visible source block.

### Compare versions and resolve a conflict

When another tab or an external editor changes the file, Lixity rejects the
conflicting save, retains the submitted draft and pauses autosave. The text in
the editor stays available. With a network error or interrupted save, use
**Versions → Download draft** to keep a copy of the current buffer.

1. Open **Versions → Compare versions**. The dialog shows **Last acknowledged
   text**, **Current file** and **Draft to review**. The last acknowledged text
   is the editor's last confirmed revision. To compare a recovery copy, choose
   it in **Versions** before opening the comparison.
2. Check the two saved texts and edit **Draft to review**. Expand **Unsaved
   text in the editor** to copy from your current working text when there are
   unsaved changes. **Use as draft** brings your candidate into the editor with
   autosave paused. Lixity asks before replacing different unsaved text or
   closing a comparison with edits.
3. Choose **Save this draft** to apply the result. The save checks the exact
   file revision shown in the comparison. If the file changed again, open a
   fresh comparison before trying to save.

The three texts use the same effective analysis settings. With automatic
language detection, the current file supplies the language for all three.
Chapter differences appear when the comparison can match the chapters. A
dialogue share rising from 25% to 50% increases by 25 percentage points.
Unavailable measurements leave the text available for review. Timeline values
stay recorded under their original measurement rules. For a new comparison,
Lixity remeasures retained source text where it can and leaves a gap when it
cannot establish comparable values.

Open **Versions → Session evolution** when you want to check what changed in
saved revisions. Its measurements load when you open it. Writing and autosave
otherwise focus on the text and the current save status.

### Use recovery copies and project backups

Choose an entry in **Versions → Choose a recovery copy**. **Load as draft**
opens a retained copy for review with saving paused. If the editor already has
unsaved changes, choose **Compare versions** to review the selected copy
alongside your working text. **Download draft** saves a separate Markdown copy
of the text currently in the editor.

Recovery lives in `.lixity/editing/recovery.sqlite3`, with up to 20 previous source
versions and eight unresolved drafts per document. Unresolved drafts are not
silently evicted; remove a reviewed copy explicitly to free a slot. This directory
contains manuscript text and must remain private and excluded from version control.
It is not included in public reading exports. Use [project backup and restore](PROJECT_BACKUP.md) for an explicit
verified inventory of saved manuscript, selected settings, research and attachments.
The editor recovery journal and unacknowledged drafts are excluded from that backup.
When the same save is retried after a process interruption, Lixity uses the
journal's verified base revision and retained source bytes to complete its
timeline. If the exact base cannot be recovered, the timeline keeps the gap.
Changes made before an autosave request reaches the server are not guaranteed
recoverable; failed/offline saves remain visibly unsaved. Browser-close warnings
are an additional safeguard, not reliable persistence. Atomic writes and retained
copies do not guarantee power-loss durability or prevent every race with an
uncooperative external editor.

| Surface | Available work |
| --- | --- |
| Local app | Read, inspect measurements, open projects, apply settings and explicitly save supported manuscript/research actions |
| `lixity dashboard` HTML | Offline manuscript and analysis snapshot; no project settings or manuscript/research writes |
| Review website | Fixed manuscript/analysis copy with the explicitly included research; no live project writes |
| Reader or companion website | Curated recipient view; no import, recalculation or local project editing |

## Explore language in the browser

Start with one question: do sentence lengths vary between chapters, or does a
passage use different vocabulary from its surroundings? Inspect the counts,
then read the passage to decide what the difference means in context.

1. Open the text and confirm its analysis language in **Project → Settings**.
   Website language preferences do not select a linguistic profile. Applying
   analysis settings rebuilds the dashboard; record the settings used for a comparison.
2. Open **Analysis overview**. In the local workspace, choose
   **Compare chapters** for the chapter matrix or style measurements, or
   **Explore patterns** for sentence rhythm. Choose a comparison within the
   supplied text rather than treating its internal reference as a population norm.
3. Return to a passage and open its measurement explanation. **Underline counted passages**
   exposes the words or sentences behind the value. **Mark differing paragraphs**
   describes a separate comparison with the chapter. Read both in context.
4. Check the [formula](METHODS.md), [language coverage](LOCALIZATION.md) and
   [interpretation limits](STABILITY.md) before drawing a conclusion. An unknown
   measurement is not zero, and a statistical difference is not a literary fault.
5. For a reproducible record, follow the [CLI text-analysis workflow](USAGE.md#linguistic-text-analysis)
   to export JSON alongside the input provenance, version and explicit settings.
   Keep samples, segmentation and preprocessing comparable across runs.

The research archive can retain supporting evidence and authored observations.
It does not automatically merge retained sources into the manuscript's analysis.

## Dashboard workflow

In the local app, read in **Manuscript** and use **Analysis overview** for
comparisons. The manuscript toolbar stays visible while analysis is active and
while you browse the overview. See [analysis navigation](#reading-settings-and-first-analysis-help)
for the overview tasks and [Style area](#style-area) for chapter comparisons.
For a separate offline analysis snapshot, see [`lixity dashboard`](USAGE.md#lixity-dashboard).

**How it’s measured** opens the measurement reference in the interface
language from the overview, evidence card, chapter inspector or version
comparison. The reference gives the counting scope, defaults and examples.
The local app serves it offline. Exported reports link to the public reference.
Read the [English measurement reference](guides/metrics/en.html) to browse all
sections.

In the manuscript, **Measure** offers within-chapter paragraph comparisons for
sentence length, function words, perception and thought cues, sensory cues,
passive patterns, modal forms and nominal-style patterns. Quoted text, the
function-word sentence filter, dialogue tags, indirect-speech cues and repeated
words show text evidence. The selected
metric's help links directly to its method. The reader separates a measured
zero, missing language rules and a measured count without exact text ranges.
Reports without paragraph evidence omit the evidence-only options.

In the installed workspace, all matching passages count toward navigation
before their detailed highlights load. Opening a finding loads its exact
text ranges for the current analysis. If the view has been replaced, reopen
the manuscript to see evidence from the current view.

Lixity computes these choices and their text ranges from the current source and
project settings. The browser stores the selected metric as a display preference.
SQLite retains selected aggregate measurements for saved versions. In the
development build, the chapter matrix uses the same chapter measurements as
the version comparison. Look for the baseline date and changes below the word,
sentence-length or quoted-speech value. Deltas require a matched chapter and the
source revision shown in the reader. Tense review uses its own saved decisions
in `.lixity/analysis-review.json`. [Revision comparison](#compare-versions-and-resolve-a-conflict)

**Quotes and marked speech** underlines the words recognized in the manuscript.
Open a mark to see how many of the paragraph's words contributed. A standalone
four-word reply can contribute all four words. The chapter bars in **Analysis
overview** show the share of all analyzed words in each chapter, so you can
compare the balance of marked and unmarked prose across chapters. A quote can
continue across paragraphs in the same chapter and scene. The evidence card
identifies the recognized marks and reports uncertain boundaries. A project's
`dialogue_regex` can declare other quotation or reply markers. The editor
labels a version delta with the date of its actual baseline.

Use Zotero to manage your source library and Lixity to retain selected evidence,
record claims and decisions, and link them to manuscript passages. The
[research guide](research/USAGE.md) explains those roles and the optional local-import workflow.

### A connected first session

Follow the [first-session checklist](ONBOARDING.md#session-checklist) to open a
project, explain one result in its paragraph and return to the text. The routes
below expand that workflow when you want to compare chapters, open a dossier
beside the manuscript, check spoken delivery or prepare a reading copy.

The [demo workspace](demo/report.html), [reader copy](demo/reader/index.html) and
[standalone companion](demo/companion/index.html) show different projections of one
fictional project. They are fixed exports; they cannot import, record or save to your project.

### Navigation model and happy path

The workspace groups controls by how they affect your reading context. In the
manuscript toolbar, actions follow one left-to-right flow:
**Reading & Presentation** (`Chapter…`, `Aa Appearance`, `Focus`, `Teleprompter`,
`Listen and direct`), **Review & Companion Dock** (`Analysis Off/On`, `? Guide`,
`Analysis overview`, `Dossiers`), and **Writing** (`Write` / `Close writing`).

Across the application, controls use six distinct interaction patterns:

- **View tabs** (`Manuscript` / `Research` / `Project` in the left sidebar):
  switch the whole workspace context. Scroll position and draft state are
  preserved; nothing is saved or discarded by switching views.
- **Context dock panels** (`Paragraph details`, `Research for this passage`, and
  `Dossiers` in the right-hand split dock): open beside the manuscript on
  desktop (or stacked with a passage-return action on mobile) so you can inspect
  values, claims and notes without losing your place in the prose.
- **In-place disclosures** (`details`/`summary`, e.g. `Aa Appearance`, `? Guide`,
  `Paragraph measurements`, `Read these marks`, `Project actions`, research composers):
  expand where they are and close with `Escape` without leaving the current view.
- **Jumps and drill-downs** (review routes, section nav, `data-jump` KPI tiles,
  heatmap cells, 3D style-space chapter links, search hits, command palette,
  research and publication links): route through one shared scroll-anchor owner
  that switches to the target view or `document`/`overview` surface, reveals
  collapsed disclosures, cancels stale reader-restore timers, applies dynamic
  sticky-header clearance, preserves focus without unintended viewport jumps,
  and highlights the arrival target (including the owning passage for search
  hits) in a reduced-motion-safe style.
- **Dialogs** (project create/open, project audio settings, `Teleprompter`,
  command palette `Ctrl+K` / `Ctrl+P`, version comparison,
  dossier image viewer): modal overlays. They require an explicit close (`Escape`
  or close button) and keep the underlying buffer, selection and undo history intact.
- **Surface switches** (`Analysis overview` and `Write` mode):
  replace continuous reading with the statistical overview panels or the
  manuscript editor. Leave the overview with `Back to passage` (restoring your
  exact paragraph and prior analysis layer) and leave writing with `Close writing`
  to save and return to the reader.

Happy path for an author or lector (no technical setup beyond the local app):

1. Read with **Analysis Off**. Use the chapter selector, text search (`Enter` /
   `Shift+Enter`) or **Back to passage** to stay oriented.
2. Turn **Analysis On** for exactly one question. Use **Underline counted passages** or
   **Mark differing paragraphs**, then return to the unmarked passage before deciding.
3. In **Analysis overview**, choose one task: **Review passages**
   (**Textstellen prüfen**), **Compare chapters** (**Kapitel vergleichen**) or
   **Explore patterns** (**Muster erkunden**). Pick a secondary view when needed;
   the next-passage action remains available above the views.
4. Follow research beside the text via **Dossiers** or **Paragraph details →
   Research for this passage**. Distinguish the exact retained quotation from
   the current dossier record; a changed source never silently updates a saved link.
5. Leave a work marker (`+ Review`, `+ Fact check`, `+ To-do`, `+ Attention`) or
   a triage/dossier decision instead of editing prose to fit a number.
6. Share a bounded copy (PDF, review workspace, reader/companion) and test it
   without the local service.

Alternative and power-user paths that reach the same features (all legitimate, pick one per task):

| Goal | Happy path | Other ways that work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chapter comparison | `Analysis overview` → `Compare chapters` → `Chapter matrix` | Heatmap cell click, KPI tile click, command palette (`Ctrl+K` / `Ctrl+P`) |
| Sentence rhythm & dialogue | `Analysis overview` → `Explore patterns` → sentence lengths or quoted text; `Analysis On` → `Measure`, or `D` (**Direct Speech Mode**) | Measure layers (`Sentence length`, `Sticky sentences`, `Dialogue-tag density`, `Word echoes`, `Indirect speech`), command palette, KPI tile drill-down, outlier stepper `◀` / `▶` |
| Tense review | `Analysis overview` → `Review passages`, or paragraph review badge with `Analysis On` | Command palette `Highlight Grammatical Tense`, `#flags` triage table `Read passage`, `.chip` click in chapter strip |
| Feature-rank projection & scenes | `Compare chapters` → `Style` → projection, or `Explore patterns` → scenes | Command palette `Open Style Space Comparison` / `Open Scenes & Registers`, `Stil` tabs (`Heatmap` / `Bänder` / `Projektion der Merkmalsränge`), 3D canvas point click |
| Passage values & evidence | Paragraph `…` button → `Paragraph details` → `Explain this passage` | Click paragraph with `Analysis Off`, click paragraph comparison badge, keyboard `Shift+F10` / right-click context menu, `?` guide actions |
| Research & quotation linking | `Research for this passage` in inspector or `Dossiers` | Select prose text → floating selection toolbar (`Link quotation`), inspector backlink card `Historical Evidence / Dossier`, command palette `Open Research Search` / `Create New Research Dossier` / `Open Chronology & Timeline` |
| Spoken review | In `Manuscript`, open `Listen and direct` for a passage preview or switch to `Chapter audio` to render or keep the chapter. [Audio workflow](AUDIO.md#getting-started) | Open a paragraph menu and choose `Passage direction`. |
| Rehearse aloud | In `Manuscript`, open `Teleprompter` to read with cues and record your microphone. [Teleprompter](AUDIO.md#manuscript-teleprompter-direction-cues-phonetics-and-synchronized-dossier-images) | Press `P` in the reader. |
| Project settings & PDF export | `Project` tab → settings form; sidebar `Project actions` → `Manuscript PDF` | Command palette `Switch to Project Settings` / `Export Manuscript as PDF`, URL hash `#view-project` |
| Writing | `Write` in the manuscript toolbar, then `Close writing` in the editor toolbar | `Undo`, `Redo`, `Find / replace` (`Ctrl/Cmd+F`), `Versions` for comparison, download and recovery, and `Dossier alongside`. |

If a control opens a side panel, it stays beside your text. If it clicks a view tab,
the whole workspace switches. If it opens a dialog, close it explicitly with `Escape`.
Surface switches (`Analysis overview` and `Write`) always expose an explicit return
action in their toolbars (`Back to passage` / `Close writing`).

<a id="reading-paragraphs-since-v230"></a>

## Reading paragraphs

Interactive workspaces start with continuous
manuscript text and **Analysis Off**. Toggle **Analysis** to reveal diagnostic
presentation in place. The switch, visible On/Off text and pressed state identify
the choice while its accessible name stays **Analysis**. Showing the layer alone
does not open a dock or collapse navigation. Its gutter marker sits outside text
flow, preserving the prose width and line wrapping. Opening or closing the
dossier is independent of that state. Use
**Analysis overview** for chapter matrices, sentence rhythm and other comparisons,
then **Back to passage** to restore the document context and prior analysis
display choice. Hiding analysis leaves the overview and restores the prior
passage tool. The inspector and dossier work with Analysis On or Off.

### Counted text and paragraph comparison

The first explicit **Analysis On** selects **Sentence length**
unless you have already saved a metric choice.
Use **Inspect passages** to choose what to inspect in the text. Use **Paragraph
details** to review the current passage and decide what to check next. Open **Analysis
overview** to compare chapters or find manuscript-wide patterns. **Back to passage**
restores your reading position and selected measurement. Changing the measurement in
the reader keeps your place in the text.

**Analysis help** highlights the next step for the current state. Turn on
analysis, choose a measurement or open a counted passage near your reading
position. **Paragraph details** remains available from the help and the
paragraph menu. Close the measurement card or paragraph details to return to
the visible help control when you started there.

In the overview, read the reason beside the first suggested passage. The
button identifies whether it opens a tense flag or the manuscript start.
Choose a question to reach its available reports and their measurement guides.

Open **Reading marks** to choose which marks appear in the text and which
chapters stay visible. Each option explains its purpose. **Underline counted
passages** shows which words or sentences were counted for the selected
measurement. Its initial state follows inline-evidence availability and your
choice is remembered per measure. **Mark differing paragraphs** highlights
paragraphs whose values differ markedly from the typical value in that chapter.
It starts on and is shared across measures. For measurements limited to
counted passages, the visible legend points to the **Analysis overview** for
chapter comparisons.
If a chapter has too few eligible paragraphs or too many tied values to
calculate a comparison, the chapter strip explains why once. Choose **Matches
in this chapter** to read any counted passages there. The strip keeps its
paragraph links, and **Paragraph details** and **Explain this passage** still
show available measurements. A measured zero remains a value.

Use **Text matches** to open the next counted passage for the selected
measurement. The count and result arrows follow the active search and filters.
Use this to work through rare wording patterns whose distances from the typical
paragraph cannot be calculated. The match's text card explains the counting
rule and offers a question to consider in context.
For sentence length, every recognized sentence with words is counted,
so enabling counted text can underline almost the whole manuscript; this does not
mean that those sentences are unusually long or require editing. With counted text enabled,
violet underlines identify counted words, patterns, quoted speech or sentences.
Hover a mark for its explanation; a short stationary tap opens it on touch
screens. Escape closes it. Analysis Off and **None** hide both kinds of indicator;
unchecking either switch hides its own marks and key. The selected measure and
switch preferences persist, including deliberate **None** and disabled switches.
The desktop app also keeps them when it starts on a different local port.

The deviation count and arrow buttons use the paragraphs reachable across the
manuscript under the active filters. Each deviation is measured within its
own chapter. When a search or filter has no matching passages, use the adjacent clear
action to keep the measurement and see more text. Text search covers the whole
manuscript. Clearing the search resumes the active tense filter. **Chapters with
tense findings** works independently of the selected measurement. It keeps the
rest of each matching chapter available for context. **Review tense
findings** opens the cues for a specific passage, subject to the configured severity
threshold.

### Explore a passage

**Paragraph details** opens chapter/source-line context and measurements in the
existing passage inspector without changing global Analysis. Its **Explain
measurement** action inspects counted text; **Research for this passage** reads
explicitly linked claims, sources and decisions. Switch between passage values,
linked research and the chosen dossier explicitly. On mobile, a paragraph-to-tool
action reveals the stacked tool heading; close or Escape returns to that passage
and its control. Desktop tools occupy adjacent space; the reader toolbar compacts
to the available width when the context panel is open.

The visible keys explain violet underlines and the marks for differing paragraphs.
Notable paragraphs have a raw-value marker with a
down/up arrow and a blue/orange edge for below/above the chapter median; the prose
background receives only a subtle edge wash. Click the marker to see the paragraph
value and the typical measured value in that chapter in the same units. The evidence
card shows what was marked, why, and what you can review in context. The chapter
matrix uses the manuscript as its reference. **Read these
marks** keeps the comparison method and counting guidance collapsed until opened.
A marked sentence's word count and its paragraph's average are different
quantities.
The **Emphasize deviations in chapter strips** control dims other paragraph chips
in those strips; it does not remove manuscript paragraphs.

Saved research has a separate visual identity:
neutral dotted marks and a book-icon **Research · … associations** control. They
identify explicitly saved quotation links to claims, dossiers and decisions;
they are not measurement deviations or automatic fact checks. The count is
associations, not distinct sources or evidence strength. The control opens
research context by keyboard or pointer; an exact inline mark also opens it on
click when no text selection is active. Closing the context returns to the
passage. Research references remain visible with Analysis Off and coexist with
solid counted-text underlines and search backgrounds. The companion's **Text
associations** control applies to the open dossier. The
[annotation design contract](ARCHITECTURE.md#annotation-semantics-and-visual-identity)
explains the ownership and color roles.

These routes share existing actions rather than creating separate records:

| Task | Passage route | Other access |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Explain counted text | **Paragraph details → Explain this passage** | Hover, click or tap a marked word or sentence |
| Read explicitly linked research | **Paragraph details → Research for this passage** | The paragraph's association count |
| Link a quotation to a claim | **Link selection to claim** in the paragraph menu | The selection toolbar or `Alt+L`, with a valid selection inside one paragraph |
| Add a work marker | The paragraph menu's marker actions | The compact selection toolbar offers **Check**; the overview lists saved work markers |
| Keep a chosen dossier beside the text | **Dossier alongside** in the paragraph menu | The reader toolbar and the dossier context control |

**Dossier alongside** displays the dossier you explicitly choose. **Research
for this passage** follows associations saved for the selected paragraph. Merely opening
a dossier beside the manuscript does not link it to that passage.

**Paragraph details → Explain this passage** also works by keyboard or right-click,
including with Analysis Off or Focus reading. That explicit action enables
Analysis and chooses Sentence length if no metric is selected, while preserving
both display-switch preferences.

The measurement card shows the selected quotation and count, the reason for
the mark and a reading question. Paragraph measurements and chapter comparison
have their own section. In **Sticky sentences**, a filled highlight identifies
each counted function word in the selected sentence. In the repeated-word
view, dashed underlines connect additional occurrences of the selected word.
Mapping limits appear under **What is counted**. A word count is not an editorial fault; a
perception-word match does not establish narrative distance. When exact
counting/display mapping cannot be verified, the value remains but its evidence
is explicitly unavailable. Browsers without native text highlighting retain
explicit inspection. Text, selection, saved quotations and search marks keep
their identities.

### Reading settings and first-analysis help

Choose a chapter in the reader toolbar. **Reading settings** groups **A−**/**A+**
for text size (16–28 nominal pixels), narrow/standard/wide text and
compact/standard/relaxed line spacing. Appearance and the desktop split are local
browser preferences; display changes do not edit the source.

The local overview opens with **Manuscript
measurements**, manuscript status, the next passage and three task choices.
Selecting **Review passages**, **Compare
chapters** or **Explore patterns** reveals one existing analysis section.
Secondary choices switch sections within that task and retain your inputs.
Use **Sections** in the overview toolbar to reach the choices again
from a long table or chart. Opening the overview again starts at manuscript
measurements, with your previous choices still available inside each task.
Selecting **Manuscript measurements** opens its overview. Deep links reveal
their owning section before navigating, including nested style views.
**Back to passage** restores the manuscript position and analysis choice.
CLI standalone reports retain direct section navigation; without JavaScript their
complete text and tables remain readable.

With **Analysis On**, open **Analysis help (?)** in the reader toolbar. It
explains the selected measure and the steps from counted text to comparison.
Return from Focus reading or the overview to find it in the regular toolbar.
The overview's opening-passage action explains whether it selected a tense
finding or the opening paragraph.
CLI `profile --help` gives the same source-lines → counted-text workflow;
default outputs and JSON contracts are unchanged.

### Compare scene evidence and rehearse an intent

Open **Analysis overview → Explore patterns → Scenes & style
registers**. Read down the two tracks in manuscript order. One shows the share
of counted words within recognized quotations or marked speech. The other shows
mean words per sentence. Each track has its own unit and scale. If there are no
scene dividers, the rows use chapters as their units.

Open a scene's detail to see how many quotation blocks are short, medium or
long and how the two halves compare. Check the counted words, sentences and
any unresolved quotation ranges before interpreting a change. Two scenes can
have the same share with very different block lengths. **Who has the floor
here?** is a question to take back to the text. Any voice entered in a card is
the author's own reading. [How the measurements work](METHODS.md#scene-evidence-and-dramaturgical-rehearsal)

Open **Story rehearsal** in the scene panel to add a card. Choose a
scene and a beat such as **Question**, **Delayed answer** or **Revelation**.
Write what that beat should disclose and, optionally, which voice it belongs
to and what effect you want to investigate. Save to retain the card with the
project. Move cards up or down to try a different order, then either reset it
or explicitly save it. The measurement rows keep the manuscript's order.

After a change to the source or analysis, a saved card can show that it needs
review. Open the current scene, select it in the card and save again to confirm
the current anchor. If the scene is missing, its earlier label remains in the
card for orientation. Use **Review scene anchor** to inspect the chosen scene and
**Return to intent card** to keep editing the same draft. After a conflict,
reloading shows the current saved order. If the card you were editing changed or
was removed elsewhere, your draft stays in the form and can be saved as a new
card. You can still review the saved cards if the scene measurements
are temporarily unavailable. If the manuscript has no chapters, open **Story rehearsal**
from the reader. The saved state belongs to the project and stays local.
[Storage and update contract](AGENTS.md#author-intent-endpoints)

### Save review decisions

Open **Analysis overview → Review passages → Tense findings** in the local
app. Expand a finding's explanation to see the configured present and past
marker counts and the criteria for a mix or a switch. Use **Show in manuscript**
to read the passage in context. Chapter, severity and decision filters narrow
the list, and **Review next finding** follows the visible findings.

From a flagged paragraph, **Paragraph details → Open review decision** returns to
the matching entry and clears any filters that hide it. Choose **Deliberately
kept**, **Changed by me** or **Review later**, then click **Save decision**.
Choosing a value alone leaves the previous decision in place. **Changed by me**
records your assessment. To edit the manuscript itself, use **Write** and save
the edit there.

Completed counts cover current kept and changed decisions. Deferred items stay
open. A change to the source or analysis settings can leave earlier decisions
stale or unmatched. Lixity retains them and counts unmatched decisions for the
current manuscript path. A renamed file has a different path. Previous decisions
for the old path remain in the project state. To resolve an out-of-date review,
refresh the analysis, reopen the finding and save a decision for the current
passage.

The [CLI review workflow](USAGE.md#lixity-analysis-review) explains the exact
identity checks, storage limits and backup scope. Reading exports omit saved
decisions. Author work markers are a separate action in the paragraph menu.

### Keyboard, touch and focus reading

**Reading settings → Keyboard shortcuts** lists the passage menu, search and
close keys and opens the command palette. In the manuscript reader, use these
keys from the corresponding view or control.

| Action | Key and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Open the passage menu | `Shift+F10` on a focused paragraph |
| Open editing actions | `Shift+F10` in the writing editor, or **Editing actions** in the toolbar |
| Save the current text | `Cmd/Ctrl+S` in **Write** |
| Enter or leave focus reading | `F` or `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F` in the manuscript reader. `Escape` also leaves active focus reading. |
| Focus manuscript search | `/` or `Cmd/Ctrl+F` in the manuscript reader |
| Navigate search results | `Enter`, `Shift+Enter` or `Escape` in the search field |
| Clear a research list filter | `Escape` in the source or dossier filter field |
| Open Teleprompter | `P` in the manuscript reader |
| Toggle marked speech highlighting | `D` when the Direct Speech Mode control is visible in the reader |
| Open the command palette | `Cmd/Ctrl+K` or `Cmd/Ctrl+P` in the workspace. In Markdown text, `Cmd/Ctrl+K` inserts a link. |
| Format in the writing editor | `Cmd/Ctrl+B` for bold or `Cmd/Ctrl+I` for italics |
| Import a manuscript in the desktop app | `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+I` from the native File menu |

Where a control provides help, its tooltip shows the name, explanation or
shortcut as needed for the current platform. Text already visible in a field's
help or button label can serve the same purpose on its own. Mouse hints wait
briefly for deliberate hovering and switch faster between neighboring controls.
Keyboard focus and explicit touch explanations show help immediately. An open
hint stays available while its trigger retains focus or the pointer stays over
the trigger or hint. Press `Escape` to dismiss it. Moving away or starting an
action cancels a pending hint. All essential actions have accessible names.
Passage jumps wait for their scrolling area to settle before a brief destination
cue; reduced-motion preferences keep navigation immediate.

Each analyzed paragraph has an **…** button. It opens the same contextual tools as a
right-click on the prose or `Shift+F10`/the context-menu key while the paragraph
