| No microphone or permission denied | Use browser site/system permissions for browser capture; use **Mic & levels** for the server's hardware. See [recording recovery](#author-voice-recording-and-listening). |
| Take cannot become a reference | Check exact transcript confirmation, 1–60 second duration, 24 kHz mono 16-bit PCM and transcript length. Prepare an excerpt if needed. [Trim with SoundCraft](#trim-a-take-locally-with-soundcraft) · [Prepare a reference file](#experimental-reference-voices) |
| Calibration or capture unavailable | Check optional host tools and the actual device/mixer; choose the device and control explicitly. Browser capture may still be available. |
| Chapter render interrupted | Start it again to reuse matching completed segments. `--fresh-audio` or the UI reuse switch requests a new interpretation; previews are always fresh. |
| CLI says audio was written but chapter retention failed | Keep the completed output, resolve the project storage/context error, and use `audio-import` with the reviewed source hash. The output may exist even though the command reports failure. |
| Audio inspection cannot compare words | Supply a timestamped transcript bound to those exact audio bytes. Signal measurements alone cannot establish word fidelity. |

### Match an audio failure to a log entry

Open the browser's Network inspector, reproduce the problem and read
`X-Lixity-Diagnostic-Id` on the audio POST response. For a render that later
fails, start with the request that submitted it. Browser microphone failures
before a request appear in the browser console. See [service logs and audio
diagnostics](INSTALLATION.md#logs) for the log location and event meanings.

===============================================================================
## docs/research/USAGE.md

Source: https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/docs/research/USAGE.md

# Local research archive

[Documentation map](../README.md) · [Browser workspace](../WORKSPACE.md) ·
[Research overview and design history](README.md)

**Local research and dossiers in an explicit project.**
Keep selected text, PDF, PNG/JPEG and MP4/WebM sources in an explicit local project. Dossiers
bring notes and evidence together; claims record assertions; decisions explain
the author's choices. The workspace preserves saved versions and exact quotations.
Text sources can be analysed separately or compared with a manuscript.
[Design history and proposals](README.md#design-history) are available separately.

Product versions describe development maturity; response, record/manifest and
physical storage versions are independent. The current reader supports research
records/manifests v1–v9, including historical records. Reading does not upgrade
record encodings. An older plaintext manifest store needs the explicit
[storage migration](#migrate-manifest-storage) before normal use. See
[compatibility and limits](#limits) before writing or opening an archive with
another application version.

For a browsable copy, use [Reading website](../WORKSPACE.md#export-a-reading-website)
in Project actions or `lixity export-site`. Research inclusion is explicit and
includes authored history and cited excerpts; original source files and full
extraction text are a separate choice. This is a static reading copy, not an
archive restore format or a hosted account with revocable permissions.

Use `lixity research --help` to discover implemented commands and
`lixity research COMMAND --help` for exact arguments and output formats.
Use `lixity about --section commands` to inspect command metadata and supported
versions in a program. Run `lixity research schema` to export the archive
entity JSON schema. For the running app and MCP, see [interface discovery](../AGENTS.md#choose-the-interface).

### Output destinations at a glance

These commands have different output objects; their options name that object.
Research human output uses English, while stored titles and content remain unchanged.

| Command | Destination option | What is written |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `research matrix`, `research compare` | `--output PATH` (optional) | Report file; otherwise stdout |
| `research canvas` | `--output PATH` (optional) | Visual JSON Canvas 1.0 of dossiers, claims, relations and decisions |
| `research extract-article` | `--output PATH` (optional) | Clean structured Markdown with metadata and research frontmatter |
| `research export` | `--output PATH` (required) | Restorable `.tar.gz` research archive |
| `research dossier ID --export-edit PATH` | `--export-edit PATH` | Non-overwriting editable Markdown draft |
| `research dossier ID --prepare --edit-file PATH` | `--output PATH` (optional) | Reviewed packet for `revise-batch`, not an accepted revision |
| `research zotero-export` | `--output DIR` (required) | New RIS/files/provenance directory |
| `research restore` | `--from ARCHIVE --to DIR` | Restored research project at the explicit target |

`--format` selects a report format where supported; it is not a destination.
Use `lixity research COMMAND --help` for exact formats and write guards. Main
analysis reports use [`-o` / `--output`](../USAGE.md#command-reference);
research commands above currently use their listed long options.

The implementation provides local captures, lexical search, exact citations,
versioned dossiers/claims/decisions, explicit manuscript associations, review,
OCR integration and verified backup/restore. It does not provide remote web
imports, embeddings/semantic search, automatic factual verification, prose
rewriting or automatic Zotero synchronization. Interface text supports seven
languages; research CLI help/errors are English. Labels do not translate sources
or extend language-specific linguistic validation.

Dossier collections with explicit reading order (`[dossier_collections]`) and
configured manuscript terms/props (`[terms]`) are stored in project configuration
(`lixity.toml` / `pyproject.toml`), keeping reading organization and lexical
candidate review separate from revising authored records or accepted pins;
see the [architecture boundary](../ARCHITECTURE.md#passage-research-presentation).
The workspace's [collection editor](../WORKSPACE.md#organizing-dossier-collections)
selects dossiers by title and orders them with move controls. Technical
identifiers remain read-only; unavailable memberships are preserved unless
explicitly removed. Collection edits do not revise authored dossier content.

## Find a task

For a first session, follow [Try it](#try-it) or the illustrated
[research walkthrough](../guides/research-pdf.html). The table points to the
maintained procedure for each task; UI and CLI use the same project archive.

| Task | Procedure |
| --- | --- |
| Start a research project and retain a source | [Try it](#try-it), [capture provenance](#origin-url-and-capture-provenance) |
| Capture selected Zotero attachments | [Zotero Desktop bridge](#zotero-desktop-bridge), [literature acquisition](#literature-acquisition) |
| Import several files or resume an interruption | [Batch ingestion](#batch-ingestion-and-non-interactive-progress), [checkpoints](#continue-an-interrupted-source-import) |
| Search notes or choose a source quotation | [Current-record search](#search-current-authored-records), [citation selection](#choose-citations-by-keywords) |
| Read dossiers beside the manuscript or inspect history | [Reading workflow](#reading-and-cli-workflows), [entries and earlier versions](#read-entries-and-earlier-versions-without-losing-context) |
| Draft dossiers from manuscript metrics | [Manuscript-driven dossier drafts](#manuscript-driven-dossier-drafts) |
| Record an assertion, its evidence and an author decision | [Create the linked records](#record-a-claim-evidence-and-an-author-decision) |
| Associate a manuscript quotation with a claim | [Exact selection, retention and review](#associate-a-manuscript-quote-with-a-claim) |
| Review claim dates or cause/effect links | [Claim chronology](#claim-chronology-and-causeeffect-links) |
| Track configured terms and props | [Terms and boundary policies](#configured-terms-props-and-boundary-policies) |
| Edit a record and handle a concurrent change | [Native editing](#native-editing-and-history), [guarded CLI update](#update-one-reviewed-record), [draft conflicts](#resolve-conflicting-drafts) |
| Edit a dossier body, section or opening text | [Markdown round trip](#edit-an-exported-markdown-dossier), [section editing](#work-on-one-dossier-section), [preamble](#edit-the-dossier-preamble-explicitly) |
| Download a saved dossier version | [Dossier PDF](#download-a-dossier-as-pdf) |
| Compare an ordinary Markdown copy with a dossier | [Read-only body comparison](#compare-a-markdown-reading-copy) |
| Attach visual references, documents or video | [Images](#keep-a-visual-reference-in-a-dossier), [PDF/video](#retain-a-pdf-or-video-in-a-dossier), [provenance corrections](#correct-retained-media-provenance-without-reattaching) |
| Describe places and journeys | [Dossier geography](#keep-places-and-journeys-in-a-dossier) |
| Review decisions and save related changes | [Decision review/change sets](#review-decisions-and-save-related-revisions-together), [applied assessments](#mark-a-decision-as-applied-to-a-reviewed-dossier) |
| Extract PDF text or diagnose a scan import | [PDF and OCR](#self-hosted-pdf-and-ocr-extraction), [local Tesseract](#use-local-ocr-without-a-worker-service) |
| Analyze a source or compare its vocabulary | [Source analysis](#analyze-a-retained-source), [manuscript comparison](#cross-corpus-comparison-and-evidence-grounding) |
| Export a claim/evidence report | [Matrix export](#claim-evidence-matrix-export), [terminal formats](#read-reports-in-the-terminal) |
| Back up, restore or convert an older store | [Choose what to back up](../PROJECT_BACKUP.md), [research backup](#export-and-restoration), [manifest migration](#migrate-manifest-storage) |
| Retire or permanently remove retained material | [Withdrawal and purge](#withdrawal-vs-purge) |
| Share a reading copy | [Reading website manual](../WORKSPACE.md#export-a-reading-website); this is separate from archive backup |
| Automate the archive | [Python entrypoint](#python-api), [API contracts](../AGENTS.md#51-research-api-lixityresearchapi), [data model](DATA_MODEL.md) |

## Try it

Install using the [installation guide](../INSTALLATION.md#cli-current-release)
or a development checkout (`make install-dev`). SQLite must include FTS5;
PDF extraction has the [separate prerequisites](#native-pdfs-versus-scans).
Prepare authorized `notes.txt` and an authored `notes.md` before these commands;
the latter is dossier content, not a second source capture.

```sh
lixity research init --project ./novel --title "Novel research" --language en
lixity research ingest --project ./novel --file ./notes.txt --allow-retention --dry-run
lixity research ingest --project ./novel --file ./notes.txt --allow-retention
lixity research search --project ./novel --query "reading room"
lixity research cite --project ./novel --passage PASSAGE_ID
lixity research dossier --project ./novel --title "Reading room" --file ./notes.md --evidence PASSAGE_ID
lixity research audit --project ./novel
```

Replace `PASSAGE_ID` with a full returned ID. To continue in the browser, choose
**Open Project** and select the same `./novel` folder used with `--project`. See
[project onboarding](../ONBOARDING.md) for the existing-project and import paths.

A new dossier without `--language` inherits the explicit
research project's language. An explicit language overrides it. Manuscript
analysis settings do not silently replace the research language, and ordinary
body updates preserve an existing dossier's language. The Python API and native
dossier creation use the same default.

Search selects current captures. Older passage IDs still cite their retained
source version. A local browser capture or a CLI ingest without `--source-id`
creates a distinct source. Refreshing an identified source with unchanged bytes
and context is a no-op. Zotero captures use their structured external identity.

`--allow-retention` permits a local copy, not redistribution or factual acceptance.
Passages stay `unreviewed`; evidence relations and author-selected claim states
require human assessment. Decisions are separate authorial records. An unmarked
`deviation_from_fact` does not certify factual accuracy. Exit codes are `0`
success, `1` operational/integrity failure and `2` usage error. Failed audits emit
`ok: false` and exit `1`; other errors use stderr without source contents.

### Capture and use a source in the browser

1. In **Research → Sources**, choose **Add source**. Choose a local file or
   enter text. Confirm permission to keep a local copy, then choose **Save and
   index source**. Use **Capture from Zotero** for selected attachments.
2. Open **Search research** and read the passage you want to cite. **Add to
   dossier draft** adds its citation to the unsaved dossier form. Review the title,
   body and citation, then choose **Save dossier** to keep the authored record.
3. To cite the same passage for an existing claim, choose **Prepare
   evidence-link draft**. Review the claim and its relation to the passage,
   then choose **Link evidence** to save the association.

Browser capture sends text for text files and preserves file bytes for PDF
uploads. For a text file whose original bytes matter, use the CLI
`research ingest --file` workflow above.

## Research workflows

Use Zotero for source collection, bibliographic metadata, ordinary reading,
annotations and general notes. Lixity connects selected evidence to authored
claims, decisions, dossiers and manuscript quotations. Historical maps and
photographs remain source material; character journeys and their scene context
are authored project records.

The research view starts with dossiers. The saved
evidence area keeps Zotero selection and optional local import behind compact
disclosures. Revision previews, historical comparisons and explicit Markdown
editing reuse the existing archive. Dossier `--file` now reads an existing UTF-8
file; migrate literal text arguments to `--body`. Archives and citations are unchanged.
Zotero is optional: retained evidence and authorized local imports work without it.

**Workspace navigation in 0.8.1:** Dossiers, Claims & evidence, Timeline,
Decisions and Sources are the content tabs. **Search research** and **Review
links** open shared tools while retaining the selected content and unfinished
forms. Search includes retained passages and current authored records; exact
quoted versions stay distinct from the current full source. Source-specific
vocabulary comparison starts in that source's reader. See the
[workspace workflow](../WORKSPACE.md#research-in-context) for return
controls and the whole-project review entry.

### Record a claim, evidence and an author decision

In a dossier, open **Dossier actions** to prepare a claim or decision in its
existing form. Claims hold assertions or hypotheses; decisions record what you
choose to do with them. Source evidence and manuscript associations have separate
save actions. In the terminal, use the dossier ID from creation or listing and a
passage ID whose citation you have inspected:

```sh
lixity research claim --project ./novel --title "Reading-room opening" \
  --statement "The source places the opening at noon." --confidence hypothetical \
  --dossier-id DOSSIER_ID
lixity research link-evidence --project ./novel --claim-id CLAIM_ID \
  --passage-id PASSAGE_ID --relation supports --rationale "Reviewed source paragraph"
lixity research decision --project ./novel --title "Move the fictional opening" \
  --rationale "Open at dawn for this scene." --claim-id CLAIM_ID \
  --dossier-id DOSSIER_ID --deviation-from-fact
```

Replace `CLAIM_ID` with the created claim's ID before the next two commands.
Each command saves a distinct record; they are not one atomic transaction.
The evidence relation records your interpretation of the source, and the
confidence records your assessment. Neither verifies the assertion. A decision's
`--deviation-from-fact` records a declared author choice, not a machine finding.
Use [citation selection](#choose-citations-by-keywords) to find a passage,
[manuscript associations](#associate-a-manuscript-quote-with-a-claim) to connect
your prose and [guarded updates](#update-one-reviewed-record) for later changes.

<a id="reading-and-cli-workflows-since-v240"></a>
### Reading and CLI workflows

Dossier, claim and decision creation starts behind
labelled disclosures, so existing records remain visible first. Evidence
association and cause/effect entry use the same pattern. Click the heading again
to collapse a form; the long creation forms also offer **Collapse** beside Save.
Collapsing and changing research tabs keep the current unsaved fields in memory.
This is not persistent draft storage: reloads and project changes can discard them.
Saving remains a separate explicit action.

Escape inside a disclosure closes its innermost open level and returns keyboard
focus to that heading. Native select menus and dialogs retain their own keyboard
handling. In the manuscript companion, Escape closes an open disclosure before
closing the companion itself. Contextual actions such as **Add historical claim**
or using a retained passage open the corresponding form and focus its next field.
Independent forms stay independent; opening a dossier in the companion replaces
the currently displayed dossier without creating another pane.

Dossier catalogue excerpts are plain-text reading previews. Markdown styling and
fenced code are omitted from the preview only, including code blocks cut short by
the excerpt limit; the saved body and API excerpt remain unchanged. Open the
record for full text, diagrams and provenance. Disclosure arrows use a brief
state transition, disabled when the operating system requests reduced motion.

Existing-archive commands may omit `--project` only when the current directory
itself is a validated initialized research project. No parent directory,
environment, global configuration or last-opened browser project is consulted.
Explicit `--project` wins; `init` requires it and restores require `--to`.
Python/HTTP project selection remains explicit.

```sh
cd ./novel
lixity research sources --format text
lixity research search --query "reading room"
lixity research link PASSAGE_ID CLAIM_ID --relation contextualizes
```

Use returned IDs. The CLI also accepts complete bare UUIDv4 selectors and
canonicalizes them to `urn:uuid:…`. The API and stored identifiers use canonical IDs.
Grouped help and discovery expose command aliases, including `dossiers`, `claims`
and `decisions`, without separate command implementations.
`link` creates evidence; `link-evidence` also supports
inspection and revisions. In the source reader, selecting text within one
uniquely resolved retained paragraph prepares an evidence draft. Review its
quote and full paragraph context, choose a claim/relation and save separately.
The citation still identifies the whole paragraph, not a sentence-level selector.
Ambiguous or cross-paragraph selections fail; whole-passage actions remain
available for touch use. Preparing a draft writes nothing.

Loading a claim's empty evidence list offers **Link passage
evidence to claim**. It opens the existing form and selects the claim only if
the draft has none; existing passage, claim and rationale choices stay intact.
Use **Find source passage** to continue the research. A claim can exist without
evidence, so **Open claim** remains meaningful independently of its citations.
Failed evidence reads show retry, not an empty list. Read-only examples do not
offer an unavailable editing route; the public demo marks it as a local-app
preview with an installation link. Unchanged archive refreshes keep an opened
evidence panel. A changed archive or project clears it so you can reload the
current evidence.

Loaded claim evidence is grouped under the
collapsible **Source quotations** heading. Closing and reopening it keeps the
loaded quotations and unsaved fields without another read. Authored search
results use **View entry** to open the current record; **View
details** on a dossier card expands its inline detail instead.

Claim choices in decision creation also use the existing evidence/relation
picker labels: title, recorded period and version, with an ID only when
those still match. The label helps distinguish records; choosing it does not
create or update an association.

In **Manuscript**, **Dossier alongside** opens a chosen dossier in a read-only
companion. It starts closed with no automatic selection. Refresh explicitly for
the latest dossier. The companion and paragraph **Paragraph details** inspector are
alternative tools; the **Analysis** display is a separate choice. Reading changes
neither document, evidence links nor the statistical baseline. See
[reader controls](../WORKSPACE.md#reading-paragraphs) for display preferences,
keyboard access, navigation and the desktop split.

Exact saved manuscript associations appear as
neutral dotted marks and a book-icon **Research** control with an association
count. They stay distinct from metric colors and counted-text underlines, even
with Analysis Off. Use the control or paragraph menu by keyboard; clicking an
exact mark opens the same research context when no native selection is active.
An association means the author saved that connection, not that a source is true
or the passage is statistically unusual. Selection and reading create no records.
See the [shared annotation contract](../ARCHITECTURE.md#annotation-semantics-and-visual-identity).

To connect the manuscript to research, select a nonempty text range within one
paragraph and choose **Link selection to claim** (or Alt+L). The
selection toolbar offers the same action; the paragraph's **…**, right-click or
keyboard context menu also reaches it when the selection is valid. Choose an existing claim,
review the quotation and explicitly allow retention before saving. This creates
an association; it does not turn a manuscript statement into source evidence.
The claim's dossier and retained evidence remain separate authored records.

For the reverse route, open **Review** in Research and use the saved manuscript
associations. **Open claim** opens the association's pinned claim revision, with the latest revision separately available; **Go to manuscript
passage** switches to analysis, reveals the paragraph, clears incompatible passage
filters and focuses the linked text. The return action is offered only when the
current paragraph hash, line range and exact quotation match the resolved anchor.
Moved, adjusted, ambiguous or unavailable anchors remain review tasks, with no
silently inferred jump or re-pin. The manuscript's saved-associations disclosure
provides the same actions while reading.

For a first read-only journey in the interactive workspace, open a paragraph's saved
associations and choose **Open claim**. Read the linked claim version, follow a
linked dossier version, then inspect its cited source passage. The pinned version
is the record the association actually used; opening a newer version does not
replace that pin. Close the record viewer, then choose **Back to passage** to
return to the requesting manuscript text. When starting in Research's **Review**
view instead, **Go to manuscript passage** opens the saved quotation directly;
that route does not create a manuscript-origin return context.
The [public demo](../demo/report.html) includes saved associations for this route;
it cannot retain a new quote or source. To save your own association, use the
native project workflow below. Source capture separately requires permission to
retain the source bytes.

Claims' **Author review state** labels map to stored `hypothetical` (**Author
assumption**), `evidenced` (**With evidence**) and `disputed` (**Disputed**).
These are author assessments, not probabilities. `evidenced` does not require an
evidence link or verify a source.

### Associate a manuscript quote with a claim

In the continuous manuscript reader, select text within one profiled paragraph. Choose **Link selection to claim** from
the selection/context tools or paragraph action (or press `Alt+L`). Review the exact quote, choose a
current claim, explicitly permit local retention of the quote, then **Save association**.
Selection, choosing a claim and previewing the form write nothing. Saving creates
a distinct `manuscript_claim_link`, with an exact claim-revision pin and paragraph
anchor. It does not edit prose, import the manuscript as a research source, create
source evidence or establish factual support. This workflow requires an explicitly
selected manuscript inside the initialized research project and a compatible
native server; standalone HTML cannot save links.

Only the selected quote, project-relative source path, raw-source SHA-256,
paragraph SHA-256, source line range and Unicode-codepoint offsets are retained,
plus an optional note and ordinary record metadata. The archive stores no full
manuscript blob. Quotes are nonblank and limited to 10,000 codepoints; notes to
2,000 characters. Offsets refer to the displayed `ParagraphProfile.text`, with an
exclusive `end`, rather than UTF-8 bytes or JavaScript UTF-16 units. The paragraph
hash is SHA-256 of that displayed text encoded as UTF-8. This established anchor
projection removes supported emphasis markers, comments and footnote anchors;
link and inline-code syntax remain as text. Soft-wrapped lines are joined and
source line endings normalized, while the raw-source SHA-256 binds the original
bytes. `find-anchor` matches the query exactly, case-sensitively, without fuzzy
matching or Unicode normalization. Use `word` for `*word*`, but retain link/code
syntax present in the paragraph text. An explicit
`--query-format markdown` also accepts copied inline formatting: it applies the
same supported emphasis/comment/footnote-anchor cleanup and trims outer
whitespace before exact matching. The default remains `--query-format display`.
This is not a general Markdown renderer: links, backticks and internal line
structure remain; heading/list block markers are not removed. Headings are not
paragraph anchors, so `# Chapter One` cannot select a chapter heading.
The returned `quote`, offsets and paragraph hash always identify the actual
displayed text. Overlapping matches also count as ambiguous: `ana` occurs twice
in `banana`, including after explicit Markdown cleanup. Prose counting uses a separate projection
that excludes destinations, images and code. Cross-paragraph, ambiguous or stale
selections fail. Paths escaping the project, including through
symlinks, are rejected. Source bytes are checked again before publication; this
optimistic guard does not lock an external editor.

`find-anchor --quote` aliases `--query`; in
`reconcile-manuscript`, `--quote` aliases `--new-quote` and retains its explicit
replacement semantics and `--link-id` requirement. Original flags remain valid.
Saving an already active link for the same claim and exact manuscript occurrence
is rejected without a write. The check includes the project-relative source path,
paragraph hash, line range and codepoint offsets; identical wording at another
position or in another manuscript remains independently linkable. A changed
whole-file digest alone does not authorize a duplicate. The existing link ID is
reported for review or revision; native HTTP returns `duplicate-link`, separately
from a stale archive. No existing duplicates are merged or retracted automatically.

Saved quotes mark only exact resolved anchors in the shared reader, in the same canonical manuscript DOM. Displaying analysis or an overview preserves
the same text and anchor model. Manuscript search still checks complete text. Review reports
changed source bytes, newer/withdrawn claims, unique moved paragraphs, adjusted
paragraphs whose quote is unchanged, and ambiguous matches. Moved or adjusted
candidates have resolved coordinates but remain pending review until an explicit
re-pin. Ambiguous quotes are not re-pinned; an edited quote requires an explicitly
reviewed, uniquely resolvable replacement through `--new-quote`. These flags
request a human review, not a semantic contradiction check or factual verdict.

Manuscript associations are grouped by their current chapter
in the review view, also when opened from a dossier's quotation count. The CLI
`review-manuscript --format text` or `--format table` shows the same current
chapter; JSON adds `resolved_chapter_num` and `resolved_chapter_title` to each
review row. These fields describe the uniquely located current passage. Moved
and adjusted candidates still require review; ambiguous, missing or changed
quotations have null chapter fields. Refreshing this view does not write dossier
revisions, change accepted links or detect all mentions of an entity. It is an
index of retained quotations, not a character-presence or scene matrix.

The paragraph menu's **Saved research**, its
saved-association count and exact saved quotation marks open the existing right
context tool. It shows up to five exact associations and their total, with pinned
claim/dossier titles and versions, author-assigned confidence and separately
labelled current dossier decisions. At most five decisions per displayed dossier
are shown with their total. Titles use the existing exact-version viewers;
**Review** remains available for unresolved anchors and the full review flow.
No saved association means no stored link for that passage, not an absence of
facts or relevant research. Opening, closing or retrying this summary performs
reads only, without retention, indexing, version upgrades or repinning. Research
setup remains explicit. This presentation adds no API or archive schema version.

The shared **Paragraph details** inspector calls
this **Research for this passage**. Quotations of the same pinned claim are
grouped under **Text associations**; its assessment belongs to that exact claim
version. The title opens the current entry, while **Linked version N** explicitly
opens an earlier pin. Current dossier decisions have their own counted
disclosure, including further decisions beyond the first five. Expanding these
details neither upgrades a link nor reconstructs its historical decision set.

Retraction and note/claim revisions use the existing record history and strict
revision API. A uniquely resolvable anchor is re-pinned explicitly: `lixity
research reconcile-manuscript --accept-moved` (or `POST /api/research-manuscript-reanchor`)
writes a new link revision with the resolved line span, refreshed paragraph hash
and offsets for adjusted paragraphs, and the current file digest; the earlier
anchor stays in revision history.

The same flow is scriptable from the CLI.
`--selection` takes the JSON selection object above (literal or a local file);
`--expected-snapshot` / `--expected-source-sha256` default to one initial read
and still fail when the bytes or the archive change before saving.

```sh
lixity research find-anchor --project ./novel novel.md --query "exact quote"
lixity research link-manuscript --project ./novel novel.md \
  --claim-id CLAIM_ID --claim-revision 2 --quote "exact quote" --allow-retention
lixity research manuscript-links --project ./novel
lixity research review-manuscript --project ./novel novel.md
lixity research reconcile-manuscript --project ./novel novel.md            # preview
lixity research reconcile-manuscript --project ./novel novel.md --accept-moved
lixity research reconcile-manuscript --project ./novel novel.md --accept-all-moved # batch refresh
```

#### Find a quote copied from Markdown

Use the explicit read-only query mode for a quote copied with
inline emphasis. For example, a paragraph containing `The **reading room** was
open.` can be located with:

```sh
lixity research find-anchor --project ./novel novel.md \
  --query '**reading room**' --query-format markdown > anchor.json
```

The JSON response contains `"quote": "reading room"`, the exact paragraph lines,
hash and Unicode-codepoint offsets, plus the project/snapshot envelope. Read the
returned quote before retaining it. If more than one occurrence exists, the
command fails; add `--line N` only after choosing the intended paragraph.
Read-only lookup changes neither the manuscript nor the archive.

For a subsequent association, `--selection` requires **only its six selection
fields**, not the complete response envelope. Extract them, then use the
reviewed archive snapshot as a write guard:

```sh
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
from pathlib import Path

anchor = json.loads(Path("anchor.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
fields = ("start_line", "end_line", "paragraph_sha256", "start", "end", "quote")
selection = {key: anchor[key] for key in fields}
Path("selection.json").write_text(json.dumps(selection, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
PY
# Inspect selection.json; replace CLAIM_ID, CLAIM_VERSION and SNAPSHOT below.
lixity research link-manuscript --project ./novel novel.md \
  --claim-id CLAIM_ID --claim-revision CLAIM_VERSION --selection selection.json \
  --expected-snapshot SNAPSHOT --allow-retention
```

Use `snapshot` from `anchor.json` for `SNAPSHOT` and a reviewed current claim
version. Re-run the lookup/review if the archive changed. `--allow-retention`
confirms permission to retain the selected quote; it does not publish anything.
Existing `link-manuscript --quote`, `--selection` and reconciliation
`--new-quote` continue to require exact displayed text and unchanged write guards.

`review-manuscript`, `find-anchor`, `link-manuscript`, `unlink-manuscript`,
`reconcile-manuscript` and `compare` accept a positional manuscript path or
`--manuscript PATH`. Use one form. When you omit the path, the CLI uses the
selected project's explicit root setting, such as
`manuscript = "drafts/manuscript.md"`. Root `lixity.toml` takes precedence over
root `[tool.lixity]`. Python calls require explicit manuscript input.

The default is resolved inside the already validated explicit/working-directory
project, never inferred from a filename or another project. Invalid config or
escaping paths fail; no fallback selects another source. Review of a configured
or explicit file that is missing/unreadable retains the existing informative
`source_state` result, rather than pretending there are no saved associations.
See [default manuscript settings](../USAGE.md#default-manuscript).

<a id="compact-manuscript-link-command-reference"></a>
<a id="end-to-end-manuscript-link-lifecycle"></a>
After editing prose: **review → preview → accept → review again**.
Use each command's `--help` for flags and formats.

| Task | Command or flag | Writes? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Check current locations and claim versions | `review-manuscript` | No |
| Preview moved/adjusted links | `reconcile-manuscript` | No |
| Accept unique moved/adjusted passages | `reconcile-manuscript --accept-moved` | Yes |
| Batch-accept all uniquely resolved links to current text | `reconcile-manuscript --accept-all-moved` | Yes; updates source hash and line anchors |
| Accept newer claim versions | `reconcile-manuscript --accept-claim-updates` | Yes; text anchors stay unchanged |
| Limit the operation to one association | Add `--link-id ID` | Follows the chosen operation |

Combining the two acceptance flags creates one revision **per association** when
its quotation resolves uniquely. Claim acceptance alone does not repair a
changed, ambiguous or unavailable quotation. For an edited quote, use the
explicit replacement below. `claim_changed` remains until that claim version is
accepted or the association is superseded.

Multi-link acceptance parses the manuscript once and commits all accepted link
updates in a single archive publication (`HEAD.json` + manifest), or commits
nothing if no link updates are accepted. Inspect `accepted`/`skipped`, then
review again. `unlink-manuscript` retracts one
association while retaining history, even if its manuscript is unavailable.
Optional snapshot/revision guards make retraction strict.

In **Research → Review**, **Inspect candidate passage** opens
the current paragraph for a uniquely moved or adjusted saved quotation before
acceptance. This also works in a read-only review website. From a dossier, its
saved manuscript-quotation count opens the corresponding filtered review.
The action checks the displayed source context, line span and exact quotation at the
resolved Unicode offsets again when clicked. It changes no saved pin or review
decision and adds no accepted inline mark. Ambiguous, changed or unavailable
quotations have no candidate action. This inspects an existing association; it
does not discover new entities or detect factual contradictions in prose.

A changed source-file digest (`source_changed`, for example after an edit in an
unrelated chapter) is informational and does not mark an association for review
while its paragraph hash, line span and quote still match exactly. An edit inside
the paragraph but outside the quote reports `anchor_adjusted` and can be accepted
with one command or click. Editing the quote itself reports `anchor_changed`;
the CLI can explicitly re-pin a uniquely resolvable replacement with
`reconcile-manuscript --accept-moved --link-id ID --new-quote "…"`, preserving
the earlier quote in history. Creating a fresh association is also possible.

Python uses `link_manuscript_claim`, `list_manuscript_links` and
`review_manuscript_links`; exact arguments and guarded native payloads are in
the [automation contract](../AGENTS.md#manual-manuscript-associations).
The native **Review** tab lists associations, anchor states and flags without
writing. Reading/listing/reviewing never opts into a newer storage schema.

Saving manuscript links requires archive support for v7 or later; it does not
downgrade a newer archive. The dialog's **What gets stored** explains quote
retention. Exported quotes remain private manuscript material; the full
manuscript is not retained. Restored links need the manuscript at its saved
project-relative path. Format details belong to the
[archive contract](../ARCHITECTURE.md#manual-manuscript-associations).

<a id="read-saved-versions-without-losing-context"></a>

### Read entries and earlier versions without losing context

Ordinary entry actions open the current
version in the shared read-only viewer. Explicit linked-version actions open
their exact pin. The **Versions** disclosure loads the version list only when
opened; expanding it never changes the displayed record. Choosing a version is
explicit. The context names the selected kind, version and current/earlier state
once; change provenance remains available without repeated version headings.
**Edit** keeps its separate draft. The browser displays
record names and source excerpts instead of technical IDs or snapshot hashes.
Reference selectors retain their exact stored IDs and version pins. When the
name of a pinned historical record is unavailable, the UI says so explicitly;
it does not substitute the current revision's title. IDs remain available in CLI
and machine-readable responses.

Read-only fields use the same localized choices as editing. Absent optional
fields are omitted; an explicit false value or measured zero remains visible.
A linked record and its pinned version appear together. **Source quotations**
are retained evidence excerpts; **Manuscript associations** refer to the
separate links back to your manuscript. Neither establishes factual truth.
Arrow keys, Home and End move between the editor's tabs; returning to Edit keeps
an unsaved draft. Reading earlier versions does not revise or retarget a record.

For daily CLI reads, list dossiers and copy a complete ID into the next command.
Dossier, claim and decision lists print complete IDs in both human and JSON output.

```sh
lixity research dossier list --project ./novel --format table
lixity research dossier list --project ./novel --tag history --tag harbour
lixity research dossier --project ./novel --set-collection characters --collection-name "Characters" --dossiers ID1,ID2
lixity research dossier list --project ./novel --collection characters
lixity research dossier DOSSIER_ID --project ./novel --section "Timeline" --format text
lixity research dossier show DOSSIER_ID --project ./novel --section "Timeline" --revision 1 --format text
lixity research terms --project ./novel --set-term "brass compass" --aliases "mariner's dial" --scoped-alternative "old pocket-watch:1"
lixity research terms --project ./novel --manuscript novel.md --format table
```

`--tag` is an exact, case-sensitive list filter; repeat it to require **all**
specified tags. It matches current tags only, preserves list ordering and works
with JSON, text or table output. It cannot be combined with a selected record,
creation or revision fields. `--tags` remains comma-separated authored metadata;
always use that full spelling when creating or revising tags. Tags remain
1–50 characters and are classifications, not aliases or unique record IDs.
An existing provenance-style tag can be queried with its full literal value,
such as `--tag "ursprung:notes/history.md"`; prefix filtering is not implemented.

`--section` text output includes the matched heading and its content, including
nested subsections. Other sections are omitted; an empty section stays empty.
Heading lookup ignores case and surrounding selector whitespace, but duplicate
matching headings are ambiguous and require reading the full dossier. Direct ID,
`show ID`, `inspect ID` and `--dossier-id ID` use the same section read. An explicit
`--revision N` retains that version; opening text never re-pins or saves it.

### Manuscript-driven dossier drafts

`dossier-drafts` inspects a manuscript and returns read-only character, scene
and place proposals
(`manuscript-dossier-drafts/1`) without writing to the archive.
`dossier-from-manuscript` explicitly creates one saved dossier from a chosen
`--draft-id` (or the first draft matching `--kind` when `--draft-id` is
omitted).

```sh
lixity research dossier-drafts --project ./novel ./novel/manuscript.md --kind location
lixity research dossier-from-manuscript --project ./novel ./novel/manuscript.md \
  --draft-id DRAFT_ID --preview-sha256 PREVIEW_SHA256 --actor local-author
```

Both commands accept `--language` to override the project's configured analysis
language. `--kind` accepts `all`, `character`, `scene` or `location`. Previewing
defaults to `all`. A creation without `--draft-id` selects the first new
character by default. With `--draft-id`, pass that suggestion's `preview_sha256`
to confirm the manuscript, settings and saved text you reviewed.
Pass the manuscript path positionally or with `--manuscript`. Omit it to use
the explicit `manuscript` setting from the selected project. The CLI reads
settings from `--project`. The browser reads settings from the selected
manuscript workspace, including when its research archive is elsewhere.
Previewing is also available before the research archive is initialized.

In the browser, open **Research → Dossiers → From manuscript** and select
**Show suggestions**. Choose a suggestion and read **Why this suggestion?**
before using **Create dossier**. The preview explains the evidence and shows
the text that will be saved. It identifies project settings, measured text
and heuristic suggestions. Character and place references use lines in the
chapter body. Scene references use their position in the chapter.
If the manuscript or settings change before saving, reload and review the
revised proposal. **Open saved dossier** opens the created record.
**New dossier** opens the manual form, where you can choose the **Character** template.
When there are no new character suggestions, **Create a character dossier
manually** opens the same form and fills the template if the form is empty.

Each dossier can contain three kinds of material. The manuscript supplies
passages and counts. Project settings supply names, variants and declared
viewpoints. The author adds interpretations and links to claims and
retained research sources. For example, read the passages around a name
before recording a relationship or deciding that a location changed.

| Proposal | Why it appears | What you can review |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Character | A configured name matches the prose, or an unconfigured capitalized name recurs in separate paragraphs in a chapter. | Name matches by chapter and a first passage. The longer report can also show declared viewpoints, estimated dialogue and complete matching paragraphs. |
| Place | A configured name matches the prose, or a repeated capitalized phrase occurs near place cues, at least once with a directional cue. | The first and last matching paragraphs and, for inferred places, a separate excerpt with the qualifying directional cue. |
| Scene or scene register | A recognized divider splits the chapter. A chapter without a divider counts as one unit. | Units in manuscript order, word and sentence counts, and the opening and closing of each individual unit. Sentence classifications are heuristic. |
| Linked object or term | The author links a configured term profile to an existing dossier. | Literal names and variants in the current manuscript. See [configured terms](#configured-terms-and-boundary-policies). |

In a generated character dossier, choose **Preview manuscript analysis**. You
can also choose **Review character analysis** under **From manuscript**.
The preview groups name counts, chapters with matches and the selected report
sections. Choose **Save dossier version** to save the
analysis alongside your notes, or **Edit dossier text** to review and change
the combined text. An unchanged analysis keeps the existing version.
Refreshing can replace an earlier generated report that you have left unedited.
Older and edited reports with distinct content remain available. The dossier
reader and PDF combine copies of the same older report. **Current passages in
the manuscript** provides complete paginated reading if the analysis exceeds
the dossier size limit.
When a matching passage has a verified target in the current reader, choose
**Go to manuscript passage** to open the paragraph. If the reader shows an
earlier manuscript version, reload the page to follow the link from the dossier.

The scene register and individual scenes can be saved independently. Scenes
follow manuscript order and show the measured opening and closing sentences.
A sentence that would exceed the dossier size limit is shown as an excerpt.
A chapter without a recognized scene separator is measured as a whole chapter
and labeled accordingly. In the combined list, a scene settings error or an
invalid place list appears alongside the available proposals. An explicit
`--kind scene` or `--kind location` request reports its settings error.

#### Configure suggestions and report length

For places, choose **Configure place suggestions** in the place suggestions or
open **Project → Analysis → Place suggestions for dossiers**. Choose automatic
suggestions, enter the
names you want to track, or turn place suggestions off. Apply the settings
and reload proposals. These names guide a text search. The dossier's
[Places and routes editor](#keep-places-and-journeys-in-a-dossier) describes
geographic points and paths you add.

The browser and CLI use the same settings in the project root.
Open **Project → Analysis → Dossier suggestions and character reports** or
choose **Configure dossier suggestions and reports** in the character
preview. Change the limits, context or excerpt selection and choose **Apply**.
In a compact proposal, the first passage remains available for checking in
the preview. The saved-text area shows the body that will be stored.

```toml
locations = ["Bern", "Hafen Nord"]

[dossier_drafts]
inferred_character_limit = 12
inferred_location_limit = 12
character_context_sentences = 2
character_report_passages = true
```

Use `locations = "auto"` for automatic place suggestions or `locations = []`
to turn them off. Leaving `locations` unset also enables automatic suggestions.
Changing the list affects future previews.
Named profiles and explicit lists take precedence over inference. The two
inference limits accept 0–50. Zero turns off that inference. Set
`character_context_sentences` to 0–5 to choose how many nearby sentences
can supplement each side of a matching paragraph. Set
`character_report_passages = false` for a compact saved report and PDF with
summary, chapter table and any available dialogue measures. The live reading
still includes the complete passages.
In a `pyproject.toml`, put the settings under `[tool.lixity]` and
`[tool.lixity.dossier_drafts]`.

The place count follows whole-name matches in prose. Read the cited matches
to check whether the same place is meant and how it is introduced and
revisited. Headings and code blocks are outside this count.

In a generated character dossier, **Current passages in the manuscript** reads
the selected source. Expand the chapter table for all counts, including zero
matches, or choose one of the matching chapters to focus the passages. The
overview locates the longest gap between name matches. Viewpoint chapters come
from project settings. Dialogue measures require enough attributed turns.

**Read the matching passages** shows each matching prose paragraph in full,
with the counted name forms highlighted. The context setting applies to
neighboring sentences that would otherwise be missing from each side.
A paragraph can contain several mentions. Read in manuscript
order or choose a chapter. Load more paragraphs to
continue through the selection. Line labels refer to the chapter body.
Configured name variants are included. Pronouns and indirect references are
outside the search, so a chapter with zero matches may still feature the
character. These counts describe the text and its matching rules.

Existing manuscript-generated character dossiers offer this view while a
manuscript is selected. Opening it reads the current source without saving a
dossier revision or creating a citation. The saved notes and exact historical
versions retain their authored text. The computed passages stay in the local
workspace, outside reading exports.

<a id="configured-terms-and-boundary-policies"></a>

### Configured terms, props and boundary policies

Configured terms (`[terms]` in `lixity.toml`) let authors track recurring terminology,
props, characters and their chapter-scoped alternatives across a manuscript. Term
definitions are project configuration settings; declaring or reviewing terms never
revises the research archive or alters manuscript files.

The **Object or term** template in the new dossier form has sections for
variants, manuscript use and continuity notes. Save the dossier, then open
**Manuscript → Configured terms & props → Manage terms & props**.
Set **Linked dossier** and save the term. Clear the field and save to remove
the association. **Configured term occurrences** in that dossier shows
matches from the current manuscript and links to verified paragraphs.
The CLI uses `--dossier-id DOSSIER_ID` for the same project setting.

In the workspace, add chapter-specific variants one at a time. Each variant
has its own wording, chapter list and note. Open the chapter picker to select
existing chapters. You can also enter planned chapter numbers in the field.
Linked occurrences use the settings of the open project when the manuscript
is stored in a subfolder.

```sh
# Declare a term with aliases and chapter-scoped alternatives
lixity research terms --project ./novel --set-term "brass compass" \
  --aliases "mariner's dial" \
  --scoped-alternative "old pocket-watch:1,2" --dossier-id DOSSIER_ID

# Review occurrences against a manuscript
lixity research terms --project ./novel --manuscript novel.md --format table
```

#### Word boundary policies and hyphen matching

Ordinary matching uses Python Unicode word boundaries, where a hyphen (U+002D)
is a non-word character. A short identifier such as `"RM"` can therefore match
inside a composite code such as `"RM-CURIA-084"`. The boundary setting controls
this lexical match; it does not change manuscript tokenization.

To address this, term profiles support a tri-state boundary setting (`strict_boundaries: bool | None`):

- **Automatic default (`strict_boundaries = None`, omitted from config):**
  Follows `--case-sensitive`. Case-sensitive terms automatically treat hyphens as intra-word
  characters (`[\w-]`), preventing partial hits in hyphenated codes (e.g. `"RM"` matches
  standalone `"RM"`, but not `"RM-CURIA-084"`). Case-insensitive terms retain standard
  Unicode word boundaries.
- **Strict override (`--strict-boundaries`, `strict_boundaries = true`):**
  Forces hyphens to be treated as intra-word characters even for case-insensitive terms.
- **Unicode override (`--no-strict-boundaries`, `strict_boundaries = false`):**
  Treats hyphens as word boundaries even for case-sensitive terms, for authors who
  intentionally want to capture substrings inside composite codes.

```sh
# Require strict hyphen-aware boundaries for a case-insensitive prop code
lixity research terms --project ./novel --set-term "prop-42" --strict-boundaries

# Permit substring matching across hyphens even when case-sensitive
lixity research terms --project ./novel --set-term "CURIA" --case-sensitive --no-strict-boundaries
```

### Claims linked to a dossier

The dossier detail groups **Dossier notes**, **Linked claims** and
**Source quotations** in one place. Its reading
surface preserves the original heading order and nesting, including repeated
headings. The section lookup does not reorder or replace the document. Unique
editable sections have an editing action beside their heading; repeated names
remain readable without an ambiguous section-editing action. Images, documents
and geography use the same reader when opened in an embedded or record view.

Open **Dossier actions** below the reading area to create a claim or decision,
or choose **All project records → Claims** or **Decisions** to open the
corresponding project-wide list. Local creation actions prepare the
existing claim/decision forms; choosing a view does not save or retain anything.

Both the research dossier reader and **Dossier alongside** show the current
claims explicitly linked to the dossier. **Open claim** uses the existing record
viewer and saved-version history. The reverse list reads current claim records;
it does not reconstruct a historical claim list for an older dossier revision.

Each claim can show an active saved manuscript-quote count. The count joins
explicit links by claim ID and the linked claim revision's pinned dossier ID,
from the same archive snapshot as the claim list. A changed snapshot or failed
read makes the count unavailable. Zero means no matching active saved link in
that snapshot; it does not establish that the claim is unused in the manuscript.
Retracting a link (`state: "retracted"`) removes it from active quote counts and
causes `research-gaps` (`lixity_research_gaps`) to report the claim under
`unanchored_claims` if no other active, non-withdrawn link remains, while the
retracted link revision stays inspectable in history (`--include-retracted`).
Newer claim/dossier revisions do not silently change an older link's association.
Counts include links pinned to other saved versions of the same logical dossier;
the reader marks that version difference explicitly.

<a id="claim-chronology-and-causeeffect-links-since-v300"></a>
### Claim chronology and cause/effect links

In **Research** -> **Timeline** (a direct top-level tab alongside **Dossiers**,
**Claims**, and **Decisions**), current claim revisions are organized by their
recorded `time_period`. **Claims** returns to the ordinary claim cards.
Each dated claim shows its placed calendar range, both sections carry a count,
and the view names the recognized formats and how to place a claim. Every period
label is preserved and the record's creation date is never substituted. Opening
or filtering the timeline changes no archive records or index.

The overview strip starts collapsed for more than twelve dated claims. Era
filters narrow the same list, and **Show more** reveals additional cards. Long
statements have an explicit expand/collapse control; the saved text is unchanged.

The chronology places valid four-digit CE years (`0001`–`9999`), ISO months
(`YYYY-MM`), ISO calendar dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and ranges whose endpoints have the
same precision, for example `1912`, `1912-03`, `1912–1914`, `1912-05-01` and
`1912-05-01 / 1912-05-03`. Ranges accept `–`, `—`, `/`, `..` and a
plain hyphen between two four-digit years (`1924-1926`, spaces optional); ISO
month/day hyphens are never split. Missing periods, invalid
dates/reversed ranges and labels such as `autumn 1912` or `44 BCE` remain visible
under **Unplaced periods** with a reason; free-text periods such as
`present day` stay there on purpose. Temporal placement does not verify
chronology or establish a historical fact. Creating or revising a claim reports
an unplaceable period in the envelope's `warnings` list, and the native claim
form shows the accepted formats under the period field.

```sh
lixity research timeline --project ./sample-project
lixity research timeline --project ./sample-project --format text
lixity research timeline --project ./sample-project --format md --dossier-id DOSSIER_ID
```

`research-timeline-local/1` includes coherent project/snapshot metadata, `dated`
and `unplaced` entries. Original periods and claim revisions remain visible;
placed entries add their parsed range and precision, unplaced entries a reason.
This projects current claims, not earlier archive timelines.

Under **Cause and effect claims**, choose the proposed cause and effect by their
displayed claim labels, review the saved versions and optionally explain your
interpretation, then select **Save cause/effect link**. The link is a separate
authored `ClaimRelation`, distinct from passage-to-claim evidence links.
`causes` is the stored relation; `results_in` is an input alias in the same
cause-to-effect direction. Self-links are rejected. Cycles are allowed as
explicit author assertions; no transitive or reverse links are inferred.

```sh
# Replace placeholders with complete claim IDs from research claim.
lixity research relate --project ./sample-project FROM_CLAIM TO_CLAIM \
  --relation causes --rationale "Author interpretation for review"
lixity research relate --project ./sample-project
lixity research relate --project ./sample-project --claim-id CLAIM_ID --include-retracted
lixity research relate --project ./sample-project --relation-id RELATION_ID --inspect
lixity research relate --project ./sample-project --relation-id RELATION_ID --history
```

New links pin the chosen claim revisions. The CLI/Python API use current
revisions when no explicit pins are supplied; `--from-claim-revision N`,
`--to-claim-revision N` and `--expected-snapshot DIGEST` let automation bind a
reviewed choice. A later claim edit does not retarget a link: its earlier
endpoint labels remain visible and `review_needed` marks newer endpoint revisions.
Creation returns `research-claim-relation-local/1`; listing returns
`research-claim-relations-local/1` with the project, snapshot, archive schema and
exact endpoint/current revision information. Retracted links are omitted unless
`--include-retracted` is supplied.

Use **Edit**/**Saved versions** or the ordinary revision workflow to correct
endpoints, change rationale or retract a relation. Unchanged endpoints keep their
pins; repinning requires explicit revisions. Three-way previews and atomic batches
accept `kind: "claim_relation"`. Retraction appends history. Archive integrity and
linked evidence do not verify causality. A first causal write opts into storage
schema v6; reads do not. See [compatibility](#limits).

<a id="choose-citations-by-keywords-since-v300"></a>

### Choose citations by keywords

In the evidence-link form, select a claim and choose **Find source passage**.
This opens the existing Search view with **Sources** selected and keeps your
claim choice. Search keywords, read the matches and choose **Use for claim** to
return to the draft. Review the full retained paragraph, choose an evidence
relation and save explicitly. Search and draft preparation accept no claim and
write no authored record. Duplicate titles are not treated as identity.

The terminal can also resolve a paragraph without typing its UUID:

```sh
lixity research cite --project ./sample-project --query "reading room"
# For multiple matches, repeat the same query and displayed snapshot:
lixity research cite --project ./sample-project --query "reading room" \
  --pick 2 --expected-snapshot SNAPSHOT_SHA256
```

Exactly one match returns the existing full `research-citation-local/1`
citation. Zero or multiple matches return the unchanged source-search
`research-search-local/1` JSON with exit code `1`; multiple matches also print
safe numbered choices on stderr. No best-ranked hit is accepted silently.
`--pick` selects one of at most 20 displayed matches (`1`–`20`) and requires the
same query plus its displayed snapshot. Changed snapshots, unavailable sources
and out-of-range choices fail; search again before choosing. Ordinary search
may refresh its disposable index, but citation selection creates no claim/link
or source capture. `--passage PASSAGE_ID` remains precise retrieval of an exact
retained citation, including historical captures. It is mutually exclusive with
`--query`; `--pick` and `--expected-snapshot` apply only to query selection.

Both routes identify the complete retained paragraph with its source version,
hash and character offsets. They do not create sentence-level citations,
translate quotations or change lexical search into semantic search.

The native evidence draft binds its selected project, reviewed snapshot and
claim revision. If these change before saving, review the current context rather
than silently linking a newer claim. Python `link_evidence` accepts optional
`expected_project_id`, `expected_snapshot` and `expected_claim_revision` guards;
HTTP evidence creation accepts `project_id`, `research_token`, `expected_snapshot`
and `expected_claim_revision`. Supplied guards reject changed reviewed context;
guarded links also reject withdrawn evidence. Source withdrawal does not erase
historical citations.

Claim lists consistently return `research-claims-local/2` with `claims`,
`project_id` and `snapshot` from one accepted snapshot. Consumers of the earlier
v1 envelope must update; stored claims/history are unchanged.

### Continue an interrupted source import

```sh
lixity research ingest --project ./novel --file source-a.pdf source-b.txt \
  --checkpoint library.json --allow-retention --progress
lixity research ingest --project ./novel --checkpoint library.json \
  --resume --allow-retention --progress
```

A checkpoint remembers ordered files and capture settings. Resume verifies bytes,
project, OCR configuration and source identity, skipping verified completed captures.
Complete prepared extraction can survive interruption/failed publication; interrupted
or unrecorded extraction may run again. Changed files/order/settings need a fresh
checkpoint. Lost completion receipts are recovered from exact accepted identities.

After another archive write, inspect the current archive and acknowledge its digest
with `--expected-snapshot DIGEST` when resuming. This authorizes that retry, without
rebasing decisions or restoring changed/purged captures. Original files must remain
present and unchanged.

Checkpoints are `.json` files under `<project>/.lixity/research/imports/`, including
when absolute paths are supplied. Limits are 1–1,000 files and 64 MiB of JSON
preparation/metadata; even one large or heavily escaped capture can exceed the
budget. Rejection preserves the previous readable checkpoint. Checkpoint imports
do not support `--dry-run`.

Preparation contains private source text outside accepted archive/export bundles.
`ingest --discard-checkpoint library.json` removes preparation/receipts, leaving
accepted records intact. Completed payloads are cleaned after publication.
Purge coordinates with matching checkpoints: busy, unreadable or malformed ones
can block it until explicit discard. Resume never silently restores deleted captures.
Progress phases use stderr; final envelopes are `research-checkpoint-ingest-local/1`
and `research-checkpoint-discard-local/1`. Import exits zero only when complete.

### Read reports in the terminal

```sh
lixity research sources --project ./novel --format text
lixity research audit --project ./novel --format text
lixity research review --project ./novel --json
```

Human reports bound long lists/findings; request JSON for the complete payload.
`audit --format text` provides a human integrity report with scope, record totals
and bounded findings; audit remains read-only.

An audit describes one observed snapshot. Saving its exact live record/manifest
counts back into a mirrored dossier creates another revision and changes those
counts again. Keep the generated audit report outside the retained research
archive and cite its observation date/snapshot in project notes instead of
continually synchronizing live totals. A successful integrity audit checks stored
objects and references, not the truth of their content or equality with Markdown
reading copies. Use the [explicit body comparison](#compare-a-markdown-reading-copy)
for that separate question. There is no separate
"stable audit" mode that hides newly accepted revisions.

Audit also verifies the complete accepted manifest ancestry.
Missing, modified, foreign-project or non-contiguous ancestor manifests fail
integrity. Its `records` count refers to accepted revision objects, including
historical authored revisions, rather than current identities or source files.
`manifest_history_checked` counts verified manifests including HEAD, or is `null`
if ancestry verification did not complete. `manifest_capacity` reports
`entries_used`, `entries_max` and `entries_remaining`; used and remaining are
`null` when the current snapshot is unavailable. At 90% of the 100,000-entry
limit, `warnings` contains an advisory capacity warning without failing integrity.
The audit checks accepted revision objects, retained source/text bytes, citations
and dossier media pins; it does not establish factual accuracy, fully decode
media or check search-index freshness.
For exact output formats and defaults, inspect the selected command's `--help` or
`lixity about --section commands`. `--pager` requires explicit use with a human format and
interactive input/output; pipes never start one. Progress phases use stderr,
leaving stdout for the result. Imported values remain inert text.
For HTTP requests, read the selected workspace's API index first. Research
data routes use JSON. Dossier PDF downloads and retained media use the
documented file formats. See [interface discovery](../AGENTS.md#choose-the-interface)
and [research API contracts](../AGENTS.md#51-research-api-lixityresearchapi).

Claim creation accepts `hypothetical`, `evidenced` or `disputed` confidence;
evidence links accept `supports`, `contradicts`, `qualifies` or `contextualizes`.
Supplied strings are trimmed and case-normalized. Native HTTP creation defaults
only omitted fields (`hypothetical` and `supports` respectively); an explicit
empty, unknown, null or non-string value returns HTTP 400 without writing.

## Native editing and history

In the dashboard, choose **Edit** on a dossier, claim, evidence link or decision.
Change the fields, select **Correction** for a transcription/wording correction
or **Supersession** for a changed interpretation or authorial choice, and give
a reason. A changed save keeps the record's ID and adds one immutable revision;
an unchanged validated save returns the existing revision. **History**
opens earlier accepted versions; it does not restore or overwrite them.

Existing associations retain their saved pins; new associations use the target's
current revision. To associate evidence with a revised claim/dossier, explicitly
change that pin in the editor. Old associations remain inspectable in history;
editing a statement does not turn its old evidence into support for the new wording.

The editor preserves failed drafts. Any archive write after opening makes its
snapshot stale. Use [three-way review](#resolve-conflicting-drafts), or **Reload
current** to discard the draft explicitly; Cancel closes without writing.

Use the [ordinary update workflow](#update-one-reviewed-record) to inspect or
revise through the CLI. Omitted fields stay unchanged; explicit empty optional
values/lists clear them. The [automation reference](../AGENTS.md#51-research-api-lixityresearchapi)
owns Python/HTTP payloads and versioned envelopes.

Source refresh never rewrites authored records. Newer-capture notices compare
explicit citations with the latest capture while preserving the original quote.
Copied text, titles and filenames do not establish source associations.

Historical dossier and evidence-link views resolve their pinned passages.
Claim and decision views show the current evidence links to their pinned claim
revision, with each link's ID and revision; they are not a reconstruction of the
entire archive at an earlier date.

### Update one reviewed record

`dossier`, `claim` and `decision` accept `list`, `show ID`, `inspect ID` or a
positional ID; explicit update/history modes still work with that ID. Their
`--latest` convenience option selects the current revision and snapshot together;
a concurrent archive change before the save still rejects the write. Inspect the record first when human review is required.

Ordinary `dossier`, `claim`, `link-evidence`, `decision` and `relate` commands
with `--update` require `--expected-revision`, `--change-kind` and `--reason`.
The archive-wide `--expected-snapshot` is optional for these ordinary updates.
When omitted, the backend checks the reviewed target revision and uses that
read's snapshot for the strict commit. Earlier unrelated writes are allowed;
changed targets and later races fail without retry or rebase. An explicit
snapshot guards the entire archive, including unrelated changes.

Add `--compact` to
`--update [--dry-run]` on `dossier`, `claim`, `link-evidence`, `decision` or
`relate` for a short receipt without the record body. The opt-in CLI schema is
`research-revision-write-summary-local/1`; warnings are retained. Previews report
`candidate_revision` and `changed_fields`; applied results report accepted
`revision`. Unchanged requests report `changed: false`, `change: null` without
advancing HEAD. Default JSON and Python/HTTP responses remain complete.
`--format text --compact` gives a human receipt on `dossier`, `claim` and `decision`.

A validated authored update whose normalized content is unchanged
returns the existing record and revision. It does not advance the archive HEAD
or rebuild the index. Revision/snapshot guards, metadata and association checks
still apply; a stale request can fail even when its fields appear unchanged.
This also applies to unchanged members of an atomic revision batch. Changed
members receive revisions normally; an entirely unchanged batch leaves HEAD
unchanged. Decision acknowledgements remain explicit append-only events.

```sh
lixity research claim --project ./novel --claim-id CLAIM_ID --update \
  --expected-revision 1 --change-kind correction --reason "Reviewed wording" \
  --statement "A revised author assertion"
```

`--update --dry-run` validates the exact proposed
write, including revision, reason, association pins and optional snapshot, without
taking the writer lock or publishing records. It does not merge drafts or promise
that a later commit will succeed. `--diff` instead compares supplied fields with
the current record in one coherent read; it is a comparison, not write validation.
Add `--from-revision N` to compare saved versions, optionally selecting
`--to-revision M`; an omitted destination means the HEAD observed in that read.

```sh
lixity research dossier --project ./novel --dossier-id DOSSIER_ID --diff \
  --section "Smuggling route" --file revised-section.md
lixity research dossier DOSSIER_ID --project ./novel --diff --from-revision 1
```

Unchanged associations retain their exact saved pins. Without an explicit snapshot,
changed associations require explicit reviewed revisions; inspect command help for
the corresponding pin options. Historical comparisons never repin. Python shares
these semantics; HTTP, images, acknowledgements and batches keep explicit guards.

For dossier body input, use `--file existing.md` or `--body "Literal text"`, never
both. Missing, unreadable or non-UTF-8 files are rejected. This applies equally to
creation, updates, preparation and prospective comparison.

### Resolve conflicting drafts

The revision editor keeps the draft and reason after a conflict and prepares a
comparison of its base revision, the current record and the draft. Under
**Review concurrent changes**, inspect the preview and explicitly choose current
or draft values for overlapping fields. **Use reviewed changes** updates the
draft; save separately. Preparing or selecting a resolution writes nothing.
Another change before saving still rejects the save and keeps the draft.

CLI users can prepare a draft with `--prepare --base-revision N` instead of
`--update`. This is three-way reconciliation of the saved base, current record
and draft, unlike exact update dry-run. Resolve overlapping fields with repeated
`--resolve FIELD=current` or `FIELD=mine`.
Submit the resulting changes with the returned snapshot/revision tokens through
the existing strict update command. Association IDs and revision pins are
compared together; unchanged associations keep their historical pins.
Prepared decision lists include `dossier_revisions`, a map from selected dossier
IDs to existing revision numbers. Keep this map when applying the preview so a
restored draft link retains the revision you inspected.

### Work on one dossier section

Bounded reads accept named IDs, positional IDs and `show`/`inspect`
with the same section/summary/citation controls, including `--revision N`.
Section and summary are distinct modes; summary and citation omission apply only
to reads. `--summary` bounds the read's body excerpt, not mutation output.
Unbounded inspection keeps its record envelope. Section edits still use
the ordinary revision workflow below.

Human section reads preserve the
selected heading's original level. Add `--body-only` to a selected
`--section ... --format text` read to export only its content as UTF-8 Markdown,
including nested headings, without the dossier title, version or selected heading.
It adds no final newline. The ordinary human display is not a replacement file:
copying its title/version/heading into `--file` would store that display metadata
as section content. JSON remains the default and keeps its existing fields.

Omit `--section` from a selected dossier
`--format text --body-only` read to export its entire authored body with the same
exact UTF-8 bytes and no added newline. Redirect output to a file when the source
contains terminal controls or Unicode formatting. `--title` also accepts a
replacement dossier title with `--update` through the ordinary revision guards.

In a dossier, choose **Edit section** beside an unambiguous heading. The existing
revision editor opens that section's content, including its subsections. It keeps
your draft after a failed save. Concurrent changes in other sections remain intact;
overlapping edits need an explicit choice in the preview before saving.

Use `dossier --dossier-id ID --section "Heading"` to read a bounded section;
`--update --file section.md --section "Heading"` replaces only that section's
content, with the usual snapshot, revision and reason requirements. Both reading
and replacing a section include its subsections. Headings inside fenced code are
ignored; repeated heading names reject ambiguous reads/updates. Other text,
line endings and evidence references are preserved. Prepared section drafts
start from the selected base revision, never a silently substituted current body.

**Scope warning:** selecting a top-level H1 can select nearly the entire dossier.
Replacing it also removes or replaces its nested headings and their content.
Use the exact narrower heading for a local edit, and inspect `--diff` before
`--update`. There is no direct-content-only selector; the subtree semantics are
the same for reading and editing.
Use `--diff --format text --section "Heading"` for a human preview that also
reports the selected heading level and number of nested headings, when present.
The warning describes selection scope; it does not decide whether replacing it
is appropriate. JSON/API comparisons and ordinary mutation output are unchanged.

Preparation can combine section text and ordinary metadata changes through the
same revision path; unrelated current sections survive. Python entrypoints and
result contracts are in the [automation reference](../AGENTS.md#51-research-api-lixityresearchapi).

#### Read, edit and verify a section

This Bash example uses invented notes in a new scratch directory.

```sh
cat > notes.md <<'MD'
# Harbour notes

## Timeline

The ferry leaves at dawn.

### Crossing

Allow two hours.

## Characters

Mira keeps the blue notebook.
MD
lixity research init --project ./section-demo --title "Section editing demo" --language en
lixity research dossier --project ./section-demo --title "Harbour notes" --file notes.md
```

Creation returns JSON. Replace `DOSSIER_ID` below with its full `dossier_id`.
Read the current section and record the displayed revision, then export the
editable content and a comparison copy of its sibling:

```sh
lixity research dossier DOSSIER_ID --project ./section-demo --section Timeline --format text
lixity research dossier DOSSIER_ID --project ./section-demo --section Timeline --format text --body-only > timeline.md
lixity research dossier DOSSIER_ID --project ./section-demo --section Characters --format text --body-only > characters.before.md
```

The first command prints:

```text
# Harbour notes

Revision 1

## Timeline

The ferry leaves at dawn.

### Crossing

Allow two hours.
```

`timeline.md` contains only the content below `## Timeline`. Edit that file,
retaining any nested headings you want to keep. For this example, replace it with:

```sh
cat > timeline.md <<'MD'
The ferry leaves at noon.

### Crossing

Allow three hours.
MD
lixity research dossier DOSSIER_ID --project ./section-demo --section Timeline \
  --file timeline.md --diff --format text
```

The preview reports `H2 'Timeline' includes 1 descendant heading` and shows
`The ferry leaves at dawn.` → `The ferry leaves at noon.` and
`Allow two hours.` → `Allow three hours.`. Inspect the whole diff, including
the unchanged neighboring heading. Compare first, then validate the intended write
against the revision you read:

```sh
lixity research dossier DOSSIER_ID --project ./section-demo --section Timeline \
  --file timeline.md --update --dry-run --expected-revision 1 \
  --change-kind correction --reason "Corrected synthetic ferry timing" --compact --format text
```

Exit 0 validates this request without writing. The compact preview prints the
following, with your full ID in place of `DOSSIER_ID`:

```text
Preview ready · would create revision 2 · DOSSIER_ID
Changed fields: body
```

Revision 2 is a candidate; a dry-run does not reserve revision 1. To save the same
