reviewed request:

```sh
lixity research dossier DOSSIER_ID --project ./section-demo --section Timeline \
  --file timeline.md --update --expected-revision 1 --change-kind correction \
  --reason "Corrected synthetic ferry timing" --compact --format text
lixity research dossier DOSSIER_ID --project ./section-demo --section Timeline --format text
lixity research dossier DOSSIER_ID --project ./section-demo --section Characters --format text --body-only > characters.after.md
cmp characters.before.md characters.after.md
```

The write prints `Saved revision 2 · DOSSIER_ID`; it does not echo the dossier body.
The section read shows `Revision 2`, the noon departure and three-hour crossing.
`cmp` exits 0 without output: the sibling still contains exactly
`Mira keeps the blue notebook.`. Revision 1 remains readable with `--revision 1`.

If another writer changes this dossier after your read, the guarded update fails
without saving. Read the new revision and use the [draft conflict workflow](#resolve-conflicting-drafts)
with `--prepare --base-revision 1` to review your file against it; repeat comparison
and validation with the resulting reviewed revision. Other dossier revisions can
advance independently when `--expected-snapshot` is omitted. Adding that snapshot
also rejects unrelated archive changes.

### Edit the dossier preamble explicitly

`dossier ID --preamble` selects the exact source
before the first actual ATX heading. It does not invent an `Overview` heading or
match a real section with that name. In a heading-free body, it selects the entire
body. Read a draft with `--format text --body-only`; update with `--file` or
`--body` and the ordinary `--update`, revision/snapshot guards, reason and change
kind. `--dry-run`, `--compact` and draft `--diff` remain available. Replacement
preserves the existing heading and all following bytes, using the body's newline
style and a blank line before the first heading. An empty replacement clears the
preamble. Whole-dossier `--body-only` requires no section selector. Human dossier
output labels authored states as revisions. Missing attachment/section targets
now list actual heading candidates; selection remains exact and unambiguous.

### Compare a Markdown reading copy

Before updating a dossier from an ordinary Markdown reading copy, inspect the
body difference without changing the archive:

```sh
lixity research dossier ID --project ./novel --file notes.md --diff --format text
```

This compares the file's literal UTF-8 body with the current dossier body. It
does not infer equivalence from matching titles, tags or a successful audit.
The report identifies the compared dossier revision; exit 0 means the comparison
completed, not that the bodies are equal. Front matter, headings and whitespace
are part of that body, so deliberate differences remain visible. The command
does not synchronize files or update title/tag metadata.

For the exact body without display headings or an added newline, use
`dossier ID --project ./novel --format text --body-only`. To accept a reviewed
change, use the existing guarded update or the exported-draft workflow below.
There is no directory mirror, background watcher or deletion synchronization.

### Download a dossier as PDF

Open a saved dossier in **Research → Dossiers** and choose **Download PDF**.
The same action is available when reading a dossier beside the manuscript or
opening a version from its history. The button identifies which saved version
it will download. If the project changes, reopen it and choose the version again.

The A4 document includes section bookmarks, saved notes, tables and pinned
source quotations, with a text summary of any saved places and routes.
For character dossiers this includes the chapter distribution and passages
saved in that version. Repeated copies of the same generated report are shown
once, including in PDFs from earlier versions. To include current manuscript
matches, review and save the analysis first. Use the dossier's attachment
controls for original media and the research view for current claim links.

### Edit an exported Markdown dossier

The archive remains authoritative. Export an
existing dossier, edit the file, preview reconciliation, then apply the reviewed
packet explicitly:

```sh
lixity research dossier ID --project ./novel --export-edit draft.md
# Edit draft.md, retaining its leading lixity-dossier-edit/1 JSON comment.
lixity research dossier ID --project ./novel --prepare --edit-file draft.md
lixity research dossier ID --project ./novel --prepare --edit-file draft.md \
  --output reviewed.json --change-kind correction --reason "Reviewed draft"
lixity research revise-batch --project ./novel --file reviewed.json \
  --apply --expected-snapshot DIGEST
```

Use the snapshot returned with the ready packet. The versioned packet binds the
reviewed project and snapshot; a later archive change requires another preview,
not substituting a newer digest. Applying reads the packet, not later edits to
the Markdown file. Export and packet output require new files outside the archive
and its internal `.lixity` directory; existing files are never overwritten.

`dossier show ID --export-edit draft.md` and the direct ID form
are equivalent. Explicit incompatible inspection/editing modes still fail.

For several related edits in one dossier, change all affected sections in this
single exported draft, then prepare and apply it once. The result is one dossier
revision, guarded against its base and the reviewed snapshot. For several
dossiers, prepare one operation per dossier and use the existing atomic change
set. Do not queue the same dossier ID repeatedly: duplicate IDs are rejected;
a dedicated multi-section patch format is not implemented.
This whole-body draft detects concurrent body edits as a conflict; it does not
automatically merge independently changed sections. Resolve the preview explicitly.

The leading comment identifies the project, record and base revision. Its
`fields` object edits title, language, tags, geography and evidence IDs; the
remaining file is the exact body, including ordinary front matter and line endings.
Keep the exported identity fields unchanged. Changed overlapping fields need an
explicit resolution. Unchanged or conflicting previews create no packet; inspect
`has_changes` and `ready` in the result. This is an explicit round trip, with no
new-record import, file watcher, deletion synchronization or automatic repinning.
`ingest` retains source evidence; it does not import authored dossier drafts.

### Keep a visual reference in a dossier

Choose **Add image**, select a local PNG/JPEG, describe it, and confirm retention
permission before saving. Caption, source title/URL, provenance note and section
are optional. Browser preview writes nothing; image capture and dossier revision
commit together or accept neither. A stale save requires refresh and review.
An open **Review links** view refreshes to show the saved revision. Earlier
assessments keep the versions they reviewed.
Saving a UTF-8 dossier body does not ingest its images: ordinary relative,
`file:` and HTTP(S) Markdown image paths are neither loaded as images nor retained.
Use **Add image**/`dossier-image` to capture and attach a local image, or reference
an already retained exact version with `lixity:image/SOURCE_ID/VERSION_ID`.

The current dossier record viewer also offers this
action. Its notes occupy a full-width reading column rather than a metadata
cell. An ordinary missing image reference offers **Choose image file**; saving
replaces that exact, unique reference in one new revision, leaving other text
untouched. Historical, explicitly pinned and exported views stay read-only.

Earlier dossier revisions retain exact image versions. Withdrawn/purged/missing
images show unavailable placeholders. Source-page URLs are metadata, never fetched.
Click an image to enlarge it. Escape closes the shared zoom viewer, which also
opens rendered diagrams. Images create no text passages,
linguistic scores, OCR or factual verification. Label generated/reconstructed
references in the caption and `context.provenance_note`; retain the actual source
of documentary photographs.

Limits are 16 MiB/image, 64 million pixels and 32 MiB for image-specific HTTP JSON.
Static PNG and supported 8-bit Huffman JPEG containers undergo signature,
structure and dimension checks, not full pixel decoding or authenticity checks.
Animated PNG, SVG and raw HTML images are unsupported; browser decoding can still
reject damaged pixels. Original bytes enter the ordinary audit/backup lifecycle.

For a joint capture/attachment, inspect the dossier and pass its exact tokens:

```sh
lixity research dossier inspect ID --project ./novel
lixity research dossier-image --project ./novel --dossier-id ID \
  --file ./reference.jpg --expected-snapshot DIGEST --expected-revision N \
  --allow-retention --alt "Describe the reference" --section "Location" \
  --context '{"provenance_note":"Generated visual reference; not a documentary photograph."}'
```

Omit `--section` to append. `--context` accepts a JSON object or local JSON-object
file. Ordinary `ingest --file reference.png --allow-retention` captures without
attachment. Python `ingest_image` does the same; `attach_dossier_image` requires
exact dossier snapshot/revision guards. Canonical destinations are
`lixity:image/SOURCE_ID/VERSION_ID` with UUID URNs. Purge identity metadata uses
record schema v2; unprovable older image associations remain missing.

`dossier --summary` keeps its short body excerpt
but reports image and media references from the entire selected dossier revision.
It no longer misses attachments placed after the excerpt.

For a paginated, read-only image inventory across active dossiers:

```sh
lixity research dossier-images --project ./novel --limit 100 --offset 0
lixity research dossier-images --project ./novel --dossier-id ID --limit 100
```

`dossier-images --json` explicitly selects its JSON
output. `dossier-image --compact` and `dossier-media --compact` return the existing
`research-revision-write-summary-local/1` receipt after saving, without copying
the dossier body. Image batch saves accept the same flag; batch `--dry-run`
continues to return its bounded `research-dossier-images-preview-local/1` receipt.

`research-dossier-images-local/1` reports exact dossier/source revisions,
the nearest real heading, source context, availability and retained SHA-256.
Ordinary Markdown image references are marked `unretained`; their destinations
are data, never loaded or imported. Code literals are excluded. `total` counts
image occurrences, not distinct sources or files; use `has_more` and `offset`
for remaining pages (maximum 200 per page). This is an accepted-record inventory,
not a scan of loose project folders or a gallery of unattached sources.
Original filenames are not reconstructed from source titles. License/credit
notes appear only when supplied in source context; no rights are inferred.
Identical retained bytes already share a hash-addressed blob. Distinct source
identities can still record different provenance; the overview does not merge
those identities merely because their bytes match.

To replace a unique ordinary image marker exactly where it occurs, pass the
overview entry's complete `reference` string as `dossier-image --replace-reference MARKER`
instead of `--section` (quote the marker as one shell argument).
Supply the selected file, explicit retention and reviewed
snapshot/revision as above. The CLI reuses the same atomic backend operation
as the image placeholder action. Ambiguous, missing or code-only markers fail
without accepting a new source or dossier revision. Existing captions outside
the marker are not deleted. Moving/removing retained pins can use the ordinary
reviewed dossier/section edit or grouped revision workflow; do not ingest
another copy merely to move an existing pin.

Storage-full/user-quota CLI failures additionally identify temporary storage
(`TMPDIR`, `TEMP`, `TMP`) as a possible cause. Free filesystem space alone does
not establish remaining user quota. Check both the project and temporary
filesystems; the diagnostic does not authorize deletion or automatic repair.

For batch attachments, `dossier-image --batch FILE`
accepts an explicit `research-dossier-image-batch/1` JSON manifest with an
`items` array. Each item contains `file` and optional `alt`, `caption`, `title`,
`context`, `origin_url`, `section` or `replace_reference`. Section and replacement
are mutually exclusive. Relative file paths resolve beside the manifest, not the
project or terminal directory. This is not automatic Markdown scanning or
semantic assignment of an image to a dossier.

```json
{
  "schema_version": "research-dossier-image-batch/1",
  "items": [
    {"file": "plan.png", "alt": "Synthetic plan", "section": "Location"},
    {"file": "detail.jpg", "alt": "Synthetic detail", "section": "Evidence"}
  ]
}
```

```sh
lixity research dossier-image --project ./novel --dossier-id ID \
  --batch ./photos/batch.json --expected-snapshot DIGEST --expected-revision N \
  --allow-retention --dry-run
```

Preview validates every file and placement but publishes nothing. Its
`research-dossier-images-preview-local/1` receipt reports planned count, byte
total, hashes and candidate revision, not accepted source identities. Omit
`--dry-run` to apply against the same reviewed snapshot/revision. All captures
and **one** dossier revision commit together or none do; another writer rejects
the entire batch. An optional per-item `sha256` binds the previewed image bytes
when applying. Without it, application reads the currently selected file bytes.
Limits are 100 PNG/JPEG items, 128 MiB aggregate source bytes, 16 MiB per image
and a 1 MiB manifest. Source identities remain distinct for distinct provenance;
hash-addressed blobs deduplicate identical bytes. This batch is for one dossier;
multi-dossier operations and an interactive batch gallery are not implemented.

### Retain a PDF or video in a dossier

Choose **Add PDF / video** in the same dossier
toolbar. Select a local PDF, MP4 or WebM, provide an accessible description and
confirm retention. Existing files in your project's folders can be selected
directly; their original bytes and paths are not modified. Source title,
provenance note, original-page URL, caption and destination section use the
same controls as images. Capture and dossier revision remain one guarded
transaction. Cancel retains nothing.

PDFs appear as document cards with an explicit open/download action, not an
embedded active document. Videos use native controls without autoplay or
automatic preload, with an original-file download alongside. Playback depends
on the browser's codecs; a container accepted for retention may still fail to
play, in which case the UI reports that failure and keeps the download.
These components are shared by dossier sections, exact historical versions,
source details and reading-website exports.

The file limit is 50 MiB; media-specific HTTP JSON has a 72 MiB transport ceiling.
Checks cover PDF header/end markers, MP4 top-level boxes and WebM container
structure. They do not establish document validity, codec decodability, safety,
authenticity or redistribution rights. These attachments create no extracted
passages, transcription, OCR or linguistic scores. Ordinary PDF `research ingest`
still performs the existing extraction workflow.
Refreshing a retained-only PDF through that workflow adds a new source version
with extracted passages; the earlier dossier pin remains unchanged.

Python `ingest_media` retains an unattached file; `attach_dossier_media` accepts
the same snapshot/revision guards and placement fields as `attach_dossier_image`.
`read_media` requires explicit project, source and version identities.
CLI `research dossier-media --file note.pdf` (also MP4/WebM) accepts the same
explicit project, retention, snapshot/revision, description and placement flags
as a single image attachment, including exact ordinary-marker replacement.
It does not extract PDF text or transcribe video; there is no media batch flag.
PDF/video pins use ordinary Markdown image syntax with destination
`lixity:media/SOURCE_ID/VERSION_ID`;
PNG/JPEG pins and their existing API keep `lixity:image/...`. Dossier read
envelopes add a separate `media` array without changing `images`.
The ordinary CLI `research ingest --file clip.webm --allow-retention` can also
retain local videos without fabricated text extraction.

Video and retained-only PDF attachments opt into record/manifest schema v9.
Older archives and accepted record bytes are not migrated; once an archive contains these, older clients
that do not understand v9 reject it. Audit, backup/restore, withdrawal and purge
use the existing source lifecycle. As with images, withdrawal hides display
URLs but does not erase retained bytes: explicit exact-version reads remain
available for local inspection until purge.

Reading websites include original files only with the separate source-file
choice. A publication profile selects which dossier/section is exposed; internal
source-context notes are not publication content. Put required public image or
video credits and license information in the selected caption/body before
sharing. A Wikipedia/Wikimedia origin does not by itself remove attribution or
share-alike conditions, and Lixity does not infer permission from that origin.
No project folder is scanned and no URL is fetched automatically.

### Correct retained media provenance without reattaching

`research media-context` corrects `origin_url`
and/or `provenance_note` for a selected retained image, video or retained-only PDF.
Use the exact source/version identifiers from the selected dossier and preview
before saving:

```sh
lixity research media-context --project ./novel --dossier-id DOSSIER_ID \
  --source-id SOURCE_ID --source-version-id VERSION_ID \
  --expected-snapshot SNAPSHOT --expected-revision 3 \
  --context '{"origin_url":"https://example.org/source","provenance_note":"Credit and license supplied by the source; verify rights separately."}' \
  --reason 'Correct attribution' --dry-run
```

Remove `--dry-run` to accept the reviewed correction. The bounded JSON receipt
reports old/new source-version pins, context and the number of matching
occurrences. A new context version shares the same source identity and retained
blob; it does not duplicate media bytes. All active occurrences of the selected
pin in this dossier change atomically. Other dossiers, captions and alternative
text remain unchanged. Snapshot/revision guards reject stale writes. Repeating
an unchanged correction creates no revision. JSON `null` clears a supplied field;
other context fields are preserved. There is no separate verified-license field:
license/credit statements belong in `provenance_note` and remain author evidence.
PDFs with extracted text require their text-provenance workflow and are refused
here rather than losing extraction lineage.

`dossier-images --missing-provenance --json` filters image occurrences missing
`origin_url` or `provenance_note` before pagination. Each entry lists absent fields
in `provenance_missing`. This is a presence check, not license validation; it
includes ordinary/unavailable image references and does not audit PDF/video credits.

### Review decisions and save related revisions together

**Review** lists structural candidates: dated/unlinked decisions, old pins and
withdrawn references. **Affected dossiers** shows explicit direct/claim-based
links, section outlines and pinned/current revisions. CLI equivalents are
`research decision-impact --decision-id ID` and `research review`.
These reports do not find every affected passage, infer contradictions, verify
history or rewrite documents. Old pins may be intentional; audit is separate.

`stale_dossier_pin` means that a saved association names an earlier dossier
revision. It does not mean that its decision is wrong or that an update was
approved. Inspect the link's direct or claim-based origin and the two revisions
before preparing an explicit pin change in the owning decision or claim.
**Mark as applied** records an assessment; it does not retarget those links.
Atomic change sets can save reviewed revisions together, but a guided bulk-pin
review or `review --resolve-all` is not implemented.

**Read decision with dossier** opens a
reversible comparison inside **Review** or **Affected dossiers**. It reads the
exact latest saved decision and dossier versions named by that report. When an
earlier assessment exists, its dossier version is separately available; the
assessment labels both acknowledged versions. The columns stack on narrow screens.
The relation concerns the whole dossier: no affected passage or semantic diff
is inferred. Closing the comparison saves nothing. **Mark as applied** and
**Reopen review** remain explicit snapshot/revision-guarded acknowledgements;
failed, unavailable or stale reads do not establish that anything was verified.

Long dossiers have a **Sections** list generated from their actual rendered
headings, Notes, linked Claims and Citations. Close/reopen the native list; a
compact current-heading link remains within the dossier while scrolling and
returns to that list. Heading links use the existing scroll/reveal behavior,
including an active source-text preview. Places and routes have their own
destination in the contents. Local heading IDs last for that accepted
rendering; saved record/revision references are unchanged.

For a human-readable daily manuscript check, use the existing explicit format:

```sh
lixity research review-manuscript --project ./novel --format text
lixity research reconcile-manuscript --project ./novel --format table
```

Reconciliation previews write nothing. These commands keep JSON as their default
for automation; `--json` selects it explicitly. No new token, UUID workflow or
writer lock is needed merely to choose a human output format.

Choose **Add to change set** in the editor, then **Review change set** to inspect,
edit or remove queued drafts and reasons before saving together. Failed/stale
saves preserve drafts for review. Drafts exist only in that browser tab and are
lost on reload. After an uncertain network result, inspect history before retrying.

```sh
lixity research revise-batch --project ./novel --file changes.json
lixity research revise-batch --project ./novel --file preview.json \
  --apply --expected-snapshot DIGEST
```

Input is an operations list or `research-revision-batch-local/1` preparation
envelope; each operation has `kind`, `id`, `expected_revision`, `changes`,
`change_kind` and `reason` (or `kind: "decision_acknowledgement"` with
`decision_id`, `dossier_id`, `expected_decision_revision`,
`expected_dossier_revision`, `status` and optional `note`; `manuscript_claim_link`
also accepts source-verified combined `anchor` + `manuscript` updates).
Preparation writes nothing. Apply validates all
operations before one commit; invalid inputs/races accept none. Duplicate IDs
and references to revisions created by that same batch fail. Existing evidence
and explicitly pinned references stay intact. A versioned preparation envelope
must match the selected project and its reviewed snapshot at application; a raw
operations list uses the explicitly supplied snapshot guard.

### Mark a decision as applied to a reviewed dossier

**Mark as applied** records your assessment for exact linked decision/dossier
revisions; **Needs another check** reopens the pair. Neither inspects prose nor
establishes semantic consistency. Later changes make the acknowledgement stale.
The UI updates your matching controls/counts after success; external changes
still require explicit refresh. Outdated pins/withdrawal warnings remain.

```sh
lixity research mark-applied --project ./novel --decision-id DECISION \
  --dossier-id DOSSIER --expected-snapshot DIGEST \
  --expected-decision-revision 2 --expected-dossier-revision 4
```

`reopen` takes the same guards; both accept `--note`. Stale/foreign targets write
nothing. Events form an explicit supersedes chain, not wall-clock ordering.
The first acknowledgement opts into record/manifest v5; accepted earlier bytes
remain intact. See [archive compatibility](#limits).

### Keep places and journeys in a dossier

Use **Places and routes** in the existing dossier
editor to add named points, paths and areas, with descriptions, periods, actors
and transport choices. Import supported GeoJSON or enter coordinates in the form.
The [harbour example](examples/harbour-geography.json) contains deliberately
fictional positions and journeys. Field help, `research dossier --help` and
`research schema` describe the supported inputs; ordinary revisions and backups
retain them with the dossier.

To enter a route in the native UI:

1. Open the dossier's edit dialog, expand **Places and routes**, and choose
   **Add place or route**. Name the journey and select **Route (line)**.
2. Enter one longitude/latitude pair per line, in travel order. Enter
   `11.10, 46.70` followed on the next line by `11.12, 46.71`. For decimal
   commas, separate the numbers with a space as in `11,10 46,70`.
3. In the optional details, enter waypoint names in the same order, one per
   coordinate, and optionally add transport, people and period. Save the dossier.
4. Select the route on the dossier map or in its numbered list. Frame the
   selection to see the whole line; **Details** opens its geographic entry.

The line joins the supplied coordinates. It does not snap to roads. There is
currently no click-to-draw editor, route playback or animated journey. A map
feature's name is not an automatic link to a matching prose heading.

Coordinates are finite WGS84 longitude/latitude pairs. The
numbered sketch and interactive Leaflet vectors work offline. Maps open with OpenStreetMap. Turn off the background or choose the sketch for
offline use; tile requests disclose the viewed area and client IP to the provider
and stop outside the visible map/project context. There is no geocoding, road
routing, travel time calculation or historical verification. Attached map images
remain separate evidence, not georeferenced backgrounds; unknown geometry stays
unplaced.

Only a geographic save opts into record/manifest v8. Later revisions remain v8
even after removing geography; reading ordinary dossiers preserves their older
encoding. Older readers cannot open v8 archives. Section edits affect prose only,
not the dossier's geographic data.

Select an object in the map or its list to read
its context and frame it. UI help and CLI `--format text` explain the measurements.
Response-only `geography_summary` (`research-geography-summary-local/1`) is
derived from the selected revision, separate from retained v8 records.

<a id="zotero-desktop-bridge-since-v1190"></a>
## Zotero Desktop bridge

Zotero owns the source library and its editable metadata, reading and notes.
Lixity retains explicitly selected evidence versions and authored project records;
these are stable captures, not a second synchronized library. Use **Open in Zotero**
to return to the source. Enable Zotero's **Settings → Advanced → Allow
other applications on this computer to communicate with Zotero**. No account,
cloud API key, plugin or additional Python dependency is required. The bridge
reads the local API and never writes Zotero's database or library.

```bash
# Preview pages; use the returned next_start as --start for further pages.
lixity research zotero --project ./novel --library users/0 --collections
lixity research zotero --project ./novel --library users/0 --query "history" --limit 20
# Replace illustrative keys and SERVER_ID with preview results.
lixity research zotero --project ./novel --library users/0 --collection-key ABCDEFGH
lixity research zotero --project ./novel --library users/0 --item-key ABCDEFGH
lixity research zotero-ingest --project ./novel --library users/0 --attachment-key JKLMNPQR --expected-server-id SERVER_ID --allow-retention --dry-run
lixity research zotero-ingest --project ./novel --library users/0 --attachment-key JKLMNPQR --expected-server-id SERVER_ID --allow-retention
lixity research reindex --project ./novel
```

Every call requires an explicit project and library. Use `users/0` for the local
user library or `groups/<numeric-id>` for a locally available group library.
Preview returns `research-zotero-local/1`, metadata and an instance `server_id`.
An item preview includes a page of attachments. Collections are paged in batches
of 100; item pages accept a limit of 1–100. `next_start` is a continuation hint,
not a total count; a final full page may lead to an empty page. External metadata
and notes remain untrusted evidence.

Capture selects one locally available PDF, UTF-8 text, Markdown, PNG or JPEG
attachment. Images use the visual capture pipeline and produce no text passages.
The existing ingestion pipeline retains stable bytes, the parent title and origin
URL. `provenance_note` records a bounded summary of creators, date, parent and
attachment versions. `context.external_reference` separately records provider,
server identity, library, parent/attachment keys and versions. This is not a
lossless bibliography export. Invalid URLs or overlong metadata fail without
publishing a capture. Language comes from the flag or project, not Zotero metadata.
Audio, video and unsupported attachments remain in Zotero. Image capture does
not interpret depicted places, extract map coordinates or establish authenticity.
Scanned PDFs require locally installed Tesseract or a configured OCR worker.
See [local OCR setup](#use-local-ocr-without-a-worker-service).

A repeated capture of the same instance/library/attachment finds its existing
active source. Identical bytes and context are a no-op, rather than a duplicate.
If the capture changed, explicitly pass its Lixity `--source-id` to refresh it.
The attachment identity must match; existing source criticism and tags are
preserved. Changed captures preserve earlier citations. A changed research
snapshot fails the operation instead of overwriting concurrent work. Titles and
languages retain the existing source-refresh restrictions. There is no automatic
background synchronization or content-based deduplication across different items.

Structured identity and safe refresh require the server identity provided by
Zotero 10 or later. An older client supporting the local endpoints may create
an unstructured CLI/Python capture, but safe refresh and identity deduplication
are unavailable. The browser requires a previewed server identity for capture.

The research dashboard lets users choose a library and collection, search items,
inspect attachments, open originals in Zotero and capture or refresh selected
eligible attachments after confirming retention. It marks captured attachments
and metadata-version changes. This indication is not a comparison of file bytes.

**Open in Zotero** uses the `zotero://` URL protocol: the Zotero installation
registers that handler for the desktop account, and the running or newly started
Zotero app selects the item. If a click has no effect, the protocol handler is
missing — for example with a manually installed or portable copy; update or
reinstall Zotero's desktop integration. This link is independent of the local API.
The local-import form stays available alongside Zotero. Standalone projects
can also import local sources through the CLI or Python API.

The bridge uses GET requests to `127.0.0.1:23119`, with a 10-second socket timeout,
bounded responses, no proxies or redirects. Files must resolve to local regular
files; download cloud-only attachments in Zotero first. Dry runs require retention
consent and validate/extract input, but leave the research store unchanged.
Temporary capture files are removed afterward. Do not grant retention merely
because a file is visible in Zotero: visibility is not redistribution permission.

Python entrypoints are `lixity.research.zotero.collections`, `.browse` and
`.ingest`, with explicit `project` and `library` arguments. They are independent
of manuscript analysis. Standard research export includes retained captures and
provenance, not the external library. Use the paired backup below for both stores.

<a id="literature-acquisition-workflow-url--zotero-reference--attachment--evidence"></a>
### Literature acquisition

A saved reference is metadata, not a retained PDF. Download an attachment in
Zotero, inspect it with `research zotero --item-key ITEM_KEY`, then capture the
selected attachment with the preview's server identity and retention permission.
`zotero-ingest --item-key ITEM_KEY` captures eligible attachments as a
batch. Finally search the retained passages and cite/link the one you reviewed.
Each step has a distinct result; a catalogue entry alone supplies no evidence.

### Additive migration to Zotero

```sh
lixity research zotero-export --project ./novel --output ./zotero-import --allow-retention --dry-run
lixity research zotero-export --project ./novel --output ./zotero-import --allow-retention
```

The destination must not exist. Export produces `library.ris`, `files/` and
`migration.json` (`research-zotero-export-local/1`). It selects the newest active
capture for each active source; withdrawn sources/captures are excluded. Original
bytes, source IDs, context and SHA-256 hashes are retained in the bundle. RIS
contains title, language, tags, origin URL and provenance notes, with an explicit
`lixity-source:<UUID>` tag and attachment file URI. Keep the reviewed bundle at
its exported location while importing RIS: attachment URIs are absolute.

Import `library.ris` through Zotero's import workflow and check its attachments.
This is additive: it neither deletes old Lixity evidence nor reconciles duplicate
Zotero imports. To bind an existing Lixity source, run `zotero-ingest` with its
`--source-id` and the imported attachment key. The parent must retain the exported
migration tag and the attachment bytes must exactly match the current capture.
Binding updates capture provenance while preserving source IDs and older citations.
A filename, title or similar text is never enough to establish this identity.

Before retiring duplicate workflows, compare active source counts and bindings,
audit the research archive, resolve representative old citations, and verify a
paired restore. A successful export is not proof that a project's migration has
finished. Preserve the pre-migration backup until restoration has been tested.

### Paired Zotero/research backup and restore

<a id="backup-scope-comparison"></a>

Use the [backup scope comparison](../PROJECT_BACKUP.md) if the same recovery
plan needs a manuscript or project assets.

Close Zotero before starting. `--confirm-zotero-closed` is the caller's explicit
confirmation. Use Zotero's **Settings → Advanced → Show Data Directory** to find
the directory containing `zotero.sqlite`. The [Zotero data directory guide](https://www.zotero.org/support/zotero_data)
explains the location and contents.

```sh
lixity research zotero-backup --project ./novel --data-dir /path/to/Zotero --output ./paired-backup --confirm-zotero-closed
lixity research zotero-restore --from ./paired-backup --to ./restored-pair
lixity research audit --project ./restored-pair/project
```

Both destinations must be new; existing directories are never overwritten.
The bundle contains `research.tar.gz`, a copy of the Zotero data directory, and
`BACKUP.json` (`research-zotero-backup-local/1`) with SHA-256 checksums and sizes.
Backup audits research and checks that Zotero files remain unchanged during
copying. Restore checks the complete inventory, checksums and research archive
before publishing `project/` and `zotero/` beneath the new destination. It does
not switch a running Zotero instance or restart Lixity.

Symlinks and special files are rejected; the paired inventory is limited to
10 GiB. External linked attachments, manuscripts and application profiles are
excluded. Use Zotero stored attachments for self-contained media backup, and
back up excluded project material separately. Verify the restored Zotero data
in a separate instance before adopting it. Open a representative stored
attachment and check an existing Lixity citation in the restored project. Rebuild
the search cache if needed with `lixity research reindex --project ./restored-pair/project`.

<a id="search-current-authored-records-since-v1190"></a>

## Search current authored records

The default CLI, Python and HTTP search covers source passages and returns
`research-search-local/1`. Select `--scope all`, `dossiers`, `claims` or
`decisions` to include current authored records with a typed
`research-search-local/2` response:

```sh
lixity research reindex --project ./novel
lixity research search --project ./novel --query "inspector" --scope all
lixity research search --project ./novel --query "inspector" --scope decisions
```

Python: `api.search("./novel", "inspector", scope="all")`.
HTTP: `POST /api/research-search` with `{"query":"inspector","scope":"all"}`.
The dashboard defaults to **All records** and offers the same type filters.
Its details button opens the existing record history with the current revision.
Press Enter in the search field or use **Search** to submit the
same query. Highlighted excerpts preserve the source's literal text, including
ampersands and angle brackets.

Source hits have `kind: "passage"` and retain their citation fields. Authored
hits have `kind`, `record_id`, `revision`, `title` and a plain-text `excerpt`;
they have no `passage_id` and cannot be used as source citations. Claim hits
include the author-selected `confidence`; decision hits include
`deviation_from_fact`. A match does not make a claim verified or a proposal final.

The shared disposable FTS5 catalogue indexes current dossier bodies/tags, claim
statements/tags/scope, decision rationales/plot impact, and their titles. It does
not index revision history or revision reasons. `all` also indexes source titles
and current source passages. Titles receive extra ranking weight; scores are
lexical relevance, not authority. Query words must all occur in one record;
there is no semantic search, identity resolution or automatic contradiction
resolution. The result limit applies across all matching types. Use type filters
when numerous source hits obscure authored records.

The browser and CLI can rebuild a missing, stale or unreadable catalogue. Use
`--strict` to require an existing, readable and current index in the CLI. Python
defaults to strict behavior and accepts `ensure_fresh=True` to allow a rebuild.
The `warnings` field reports a successful refresh. It also suggests `--scope all`
when the default `sources` search returns no passage hits. The
[data model](DATA_MODEL.md#search-database-and-deletion) describes the snapshot
and transaction checks that back these results.

### Batch ingestion and non-interactive progress

- **Batch ingest**: Pass multiple files to `lixity research ingest --project ./p --file a.pdf b.txt --allow-retention`.
  It returns `research-batch-ingest-local/1` detailing per-item outcomes (`succeeded`, `failed`, `items`), ensuring
  partial batch success is preserved even if one file fails validation.
- **Progress reporting**: Add `--progress` to `ingest` or `zotero-ingest`. Phase notifications with elapsed
  seconds are streamed to `stderr`, keeping `stdout` strictly machine-readable JSON.
  These are phase-boundary notifications, not periodic heartbeats, JSONL events
  or a per-page stream during worker inference.

<a id="section-bounded-dossier-inspection-and-revision"></a>
For bounded dossier reads/edits use the [section workflow](#work-on-one-dossier-section).

### Claim-evidence matrix export

`research matrix --format md|csv|json` connects claims, evidence, dossiers and
decisions. The dashboard and HTTP export use the same report. Support counts
summarize authored links, and `deviation_from_fact` records an author's explicit
choice; neither is a factual truth score.

## Python API

```python
from lixity.research import api

api.init("./novel", title="Novel research", language="en")
capture = api.ingest("./novel", "notes.txt", allow_retention=True)
results = api.search("./novel", "reading room", limit=5)
# Inspect a returned passage before using api.cite or linking it to a claim.
```

The project argument is mandatory; research discovers no manuscript and reads no
analysis thresholds. `lixity build` neither imports sources nor refreshes research
indexes. The [automation reference](../AGENTS.md#51-research-api-lixityresearchapi)
covers public entrypoints and envelopes.

## Analyze a retained source

Use the explicit source ID returned by `research sources` to analyze retained
text independently of the manuscript:

```sh
lixity research analyze --project ./novel --source-id SOURCE_ID
lixity research dashboard --project ./novel --source-id SOURCE_ID > source-report.html
```

The first command returns JSON; the second writes a standalone HTML report to
stdout. Add `--version-id VERSION_ID` to inspect an earlier available capture. Retained images, videos and PDFs attached without extraction have no text
analysis. To compare source vocabulary with a manuscript, use the separate
comparison workflow below.

Source analysis uses the shared engine, selected archived version/language and
explicit overrides. Its interpretation is `source_internal`, with
`context_status: user_supplied_unverified`; manuscript settings are not inherited.
`baseline_coverage.estimable_features` counts features whose standardized
comparison is available under the active style schema, excluding insufficient
chapter samples and zero-MAD references.
Period, place, genre, translation and language context do not validate a source or
make it a manuscript style baseline. Local title/tag filters search only loaded
metadata; use archive search for retained text.

### Cross-corpus comparison and evidence grounding

`compare` requires an explicit source and manuscript. In the workspace, open
**Research → Sources**, select a retained text source, then choose
**Compare vocabulary with manuscript**. The action compares the current source
capture with the loaded manuscript. Open a pinned quotation to read its exact
historical version.
The CLI accepts the manuscript as a positional path or via `--manuscript`.
Omit it when `--project` points to a project with an explicit manuscript
setting.

The comparison produces a separate report. With matching resolved language
profiles it measures lexical Jaccard/overlap, shared/exclusive terms, signed full
$2\times2$ Dunning $G^2$ keyness, register contrasts and per-chapter occurrences
per 1,000 words. Grounding describes where source vocabulary occurs in the
manuscript. Factual support and chronology require review of the evidence itself.
The term-list limit controls the number of reported rows.

```sh
lixity research compare --project ./novel ./novel/manuscript.md --source-id SOURCE_ID \
  --format md --output ./grounding-report.md
```

Counts share core prose scope: body paragraphs, lists and blockquotes, excluding
code/comments/footnote definitions. With chapters, headings/front matter/appendix
are excluded; otherwise remaining document prose is used. Comparison uses code-
default parsing and the archived source language; it does not inherit custom
project `chapter_regex`/`appendix_marker`. Inspect the chapter trace before
comparing with a differently configured dashboard.

The CLI uses explicit `--language` first, otherwise the selected
project's root-local `language`, otherwise English. Root `lixity.toml` overrides
root `[tool.lixity]`; ancestor, user and nested manuscript settings are excluded.
The archive's project language is not a fallback for a missing analysis setting.
Use `--language auto` to request detection explicitly, or set
`language = "auto"` in the selected root. A required malformed, unreadable or invalid language
configuration fails instead of silently using English or `generic`. Supplying
both a manuscript path and `--language` needs no project configuration read.
The Python API keeps its English default unless `language` is supplied. Check
the returned `manuscript_language`, `lexical_comparable` and comparison limits.

A profile match indicates that both inputs use the same counting rules. Two
`generic` inputs can contain different languages. When the resolved profiles
differ, the comparison (`schema_version: "research-comparison-local/2"`) keeps
per-side raw counts (`source_tokens`, `source_content_words`,
`manuscript_tokens`, `manuscript_content_words`, `source_vocabulary_types`,
`manuscript_vocabulary_types`, per-chapter `words` and `content_words`, and
per-side `register_contrast` measurements), sets `meta.lexical_comparable: false`
and `cross_language_lexical_comparison` in `comparison_limits`, and returns
`null` / `[]` for cross-corpus lexical overlap and similarity
(`shared_types`, `source_exclusive_types`, `manuscript_exclusive_types`,
`jaccard_similarity`, `overlap_coefficient`, `top_shared_terms`,
`top_source_exclusive`), Dunning $G^2$ keyness lists (`source_key_terms`,
`manuscript_key_terms`), `register_contrast[*].delta`, and per-chapter
`overlap_types`, `overlap_tokens`, `grounding_density`, `top_terms`, and
`key_terms_present`. The Markdown renderer displays `–` for those unavailable
cells alongside the limitation notice. Historical `research-comparison-local/1`
outputs remain valid in saved exports, while live comparisons emit `/2`.
Guiraud/register contrasts depend on length, language and discourse mode.
Matching a source is not a writing-quality objective.

## Storage, lifecycle and recovery

Keep the accepted store and its backups intact. Use [Export and restoration](#export-and-restoration)
for backup verification and the [local data model](DATA_MODEL.md#authority-and-identity)
when inspecting archive files.

- `research/project.json`: immutable initial project configuration.
- `research/revisions/`: immutable, schema-checked records.
- `research/blobs/`: SHA-256-addressed original source bytes and extracted text; originals are not normalized.
- `research/manifests/`: complete, gzip-compressed snapshots; `research/HEAD.json` selects one.
- `research/storage.json`: physical storage layout marker; canonical JSON hashes remain unchanged.
- `.lixity/research/`: disposable catalogue and writer lock.

### Withdrawal vs. purge

- **Withdrawal (`withdraw`)**: Preserves the audit trail and archived source text,
  records a tombstone in the manifest, excludes the source or version from default
  search, and marks existing citations as `availability: "withdrawn"`. Analysis
  fails closed for withdrawn sources.
- **Purge (`purge`)**: Permanently removes source records, extraction records,
  and passage records from the store and unlinks unshared original blobs. Citations
  for purged passages fail closed with `ResearchError`. Supports `--dry-run` to preview
  affected records and blobs before deletion. Authored dossiers and evidence
  links remain for their audit trail, but their purged citations are marked
  `availability: "purged"` and expose no deleted quotation text.

Original files and extracted text can share exact bytes across sources. The
purge plan checks both kinds of blob reference, preserves shared bytes and
removes unshared extraction text as well as originals. A dry run's
`deleted_blobs` lists the files it would remove.

`withdraw` also retires a dossier through the same
tombstone mechanism. In the active dossier details or current revision viewer,
choose **Withdraw dossier**, review the effect and confirm. **Discard draft**
in **New dossier** and **Discard changes** in the revision editor clear the
unsaved form. For the CLI, inspect the revision and snapshot, preview, then
repeat the command without `--dry-run` to accept the retirement:

```sh
lixity research dossier inspect DOSSIER_ID --project ./novel
lixity research withdraw --project ./novel --dossier-id DOSSIER_ID \
  --expected-revision REVISION --expected-snapshot SNAPSHOT \
  --reason "Consolidated into the reviewed dossier" --dry-run
```

Both guards must still match when saving. The dossier disappears from active
lists and search; its bytes, evidence, associations and backups remain. Explicit
revision reads, history and saved-revision comparisons remain available and
identify the withdrawal. Current reads, edits, new associations/repins, image
attachments and fresh acknowledgements reject retired dossiers. Existing pins
survive unrelated revisions of linked records.

`supersession` describes an ordinary revision's intent; it does not retire a
dossier. Retirement does not create a replacement link or merge records. Source
withdrawal and purge keep their existing contracts.

## Export and restoration

Use this archive to recover accepted research. To recover a manuscript and its
research together, use [project backup and restore](../PROJECT_BACKUP.md).

```sh
lixity research export --project ./novel --output ./backup-novel.tar.gz
lixity research restore --from ./backup-novel.tar.gz --to ./restored-novel
lixity research audit --project ./restored-novel
```

Export packages accepted history, manifests and retained source bytes. A root
`lixity.toml`, when present, is included whole after validation. Review it for
credentials and machine-specific paths before sharing an archive. Manuscripts,
`pyproject.toml`, search indexes, locks, Zotero and application profiles are
outside this archive's scope. The [paired backup](#paired-zoteroresearch-backup-and-restore)
adds the Zotero data directory.

`EXPORT_MANIFEST.json` records SHA-256 and byte lengths. Restore requires a new
or empty directory and validates paths, checksums, sizes, contiguous history and
project identity before publishing the store. The `research/` directory and any
included `lixity.toml` are placed separately. Inspect the destination before
retrying if publication reports an error. Rebuild the disposable index when
needed with `lixity research reindex --project ./restored-novel`.

Choose a new output outside `research/` and `.lixity/research/`. Export can
replace an existing file. It holds the project writer lock while copying the
accepted snapshot into a verified candidate and enforces the 10 GiB uncompressed
limit, including the manifest. A failure before replacement preserves the
previous output. If the command reports publication with uncertain durability,
inspect and restore-test that output before retrying. The [archive model](DATA_MODEL.md#backup-validation-and-publication)
describes backup validation and publication. Verify a restored copy with an
audit and a representative retained citation.

### Recover from an interrupted write

Use the reported outcome to decide how to continue. See the [write state reference](DATA_MODEL.md#validation-and-publication).

| Reported outcome | Next step |
| --- | --- |
| Writer busy | Let the current operation finish, then preview again. For permission or read-only errors, resolve the filesystem problem first. The lock file can exist while idle. |
| Reviewed snapshot changed | Reload and review the affected content before accepting with the new snapshot. |
| Publication uncertain | Preserve the store. Reload and audit the accepted snapshot before making another write. |
| Accepted snapshot, cleanup pending | Check the reported filesystem error and the named unreferenced files. Copies in independent backups or filesystem snapshots remain subject to their own retention policies. |
| Initialization interrupted | Preserve the incomplete directory for inspection. Initialization refuses to overwrite it. |

A later save can preserve an interrupted edit's valid next revision under a
content-addressed `.unpublished` filename. Review these files as recovery
material. The selected HEAD determines which revisions are accepted.

### Migrate manifest storage

New archives use compressed manifest storage. For an existing uncompressed
project, migrate explicitly before normal use.

```sh
lixity research migrate-storage --project ./novel \
  --backup ./backups/novel-before-manifest-compression.tar.gz --json
```

Stop every service/writer using that project first. The backup must be outside
`research/` and `.lixity/research/`; an existing backup is never overwritten.
An optional `--expected-snapshot HASH` binds the migration to the reviewed HEAD.
The migration verifies a restored backup, rechecks HEAD under the writer lock,
stages and verifies all accepted compressed manifests, then atomically publishes
the layout marker. Only verified accepted plaintext duplicates are removed.
HEAD, canonical manifest hashes, authored revisions, media and retained source
bytes stay unchanged. Interrupted staging leaves plaintext authoritative;
interrupted cleanup leaves a valid compressed store and can be retried using
the same verified backup. Unrelated recovery objects are not deleted.

Keep enough free space for the backup, its temporary restored copy and compressed
manifests before plaintext is reclaimed. The receipt reports original/compressed
manifest bytes and unchanged snapshot. Portable backups retain the existing
`research-export-local/1` transport with canonical `.json` members; restore
converts unpublished staging into current compressed storage before publication.
This reduces manifest bytes but does not introduce deltas or remove the 100,000
revision-entry ceiling. Old program versions cannot open the new physical layout;
rollback requires stopping writers and restoring the complete pre-migration
backup with the intended program version. Restart with the current installation
and audit after migration. There is one current storage/UI path, no compatibility
mode to select.

## Origin URL and capture provenance

Optional `--origin-url` / `origin_url=` is retained as
`SourceVersion.context.origin_url`, independently of title, tags and
`provenance_note`. Source details, lists and citation context expose it.
Refreshing identical PDF bytes verifies and reuses retained original/extracted
blobs and passage spans. Metadata-only changes create a new capture without
rerunning OCR; identical bytes/context remain a no-op. Earlier citations keep
their original capture.

```sh
lixity research ingest --project ./novel --file ./notes.txt --allow-retention \
  --origin-url https://example.org/archive/notes
```

The URL must be absolute HTTP(S), at most 2,000 characters, without credentials,
whitespace or control characters. It is stored as submitted, never requested or
used to accept a claim. Prefer stable source addresses over signed links with
private query tokens. The browser displays it as escaped text. Choose a local
file or pasted text for each import. If both contain data, the form asks you to
choose and retains both. Failed imports and edits made while
an import is in progress remain in the form. On success, only an unchanged
submitted form is cleared. The local importer remains available alongside Zotero.

On refresh, an omitted `origin_url` retains the context selected by the existing
API: supplied `context`, or the latest capture's context when omitted. An explicit
URL overrides `context.origin_url`. Changing only the URL creates a new capture;
identical bytes and context remain a no-op. To clear a URL deliberately, supply a
context mapping with `origin_url: null` (and any other metadata to retain).
Earlier citations resolve their own capture and retain the original URL. URLs,
filenames and titles never establish source identity automatically.

URL-bearing captures require schema v2, or v3 when carrying structured Zotero
identity. Capture sequence is distinct from authored-record revision history.
Earlier URL-free records retain their encoding. See [compatibility](#limits).

## Self-hosted PDF and OCR extraction

PDF ingestion retains the original PDF bytes and extracted UTF-8 text as
separate content-addressed blobs:

```sh
lixity research ingest --project ./novel --file ./document.pdf --allow-retention
```

The browser file input also accepts binary PDFs. It reads the selected file as base64 for transport and passes the decoded
bytes through the same import API as text and server-local files. The browser
shows reading/extraction/completion states and prevents duplicate submits while
waiting. This is not a streamed per-page progress feed.
Successful local and Zotero captures also show returned warnings in the import
status. Read those messages; a successful capture is not proof of OCR accuracy.

### Native PDFs versus scans

Install local Poppler tools: `poppler-utils` on Debian/Ubuntu, or `poppler` with
Homebrew. Both `pdftotext` and `pdftoppm` must be visible on the server's PATH.
`pdftoppm` rasterizes physical pages at 150 dpi for native/worker extraction
and 300 dpi for Tesseract; `pdftotext` extracts text layers.
Without page rasterization, the configured scan worker cannot receive normal
page inputs. Native text extraction may still work when the page count can be
determined; `partial` does not indicate a complete OCR setup.

An image-only scan has no usable text layer. Select
[local Tesseract](#use-local-ocr-without-a-worker-service) or a configured
self-hosted worker; Lixity does not install their engines, language data or
models. Run diagnostics in the same environment as the server:

```sh
lixity research ocr-status [--worker-cmd PATH] [--probe]
```

`--probe` (HTTP `?probe=1`) executes a synthetic worker/Tesseract request and
reports execution/latency; native mode has no worker to probe. Success upgrades
only `ready` to `ready (probed)`, never invalid configuration or `partial`.
Inspect `probe.ok` and configuration/dependencies together: the diagnostic CLI
exits `0` even when a probe fails.

The same information is available at `GET /api/research/ocr-status` and in
`GET /api/research/status`. The dashboard maps these codes to localized labels:

| Code | Configuration detected | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ready` / `ready (probed)` | Selected worker or Tesseract with requested language data, plus pdftoppm | Test an authorized scan and inspect extracted text |
| `native_only` | Native extraction with both Poppler tools | Native PDFs work; select Tesseract or a worker for scans |
| `partial` | Extraction/OCR engine available, pdftoppm missing | Install the rasterizer before multi-page use |
| `misconfigured_worker` | Worker absent/not executable, invalid timeout, or failed probe | Check worker path, permissions, service environment and `LIXITY_OCR_TIMEOUT` |
| `misconfigured_backend` | Invalid backend/native timeout, or unavailable Tesseract/language data | Check `LIXITY_OCR_BACKEND`, `LIXITY_OCR_LANGUAGES`, timeout and local installation |
| `missing_dependencies` | No complete usable setup | Install Poppler and select a scan backend when needed |

Diagnostics establish executable availability; a probe establishes only that
request's execution. Neither verifies model weights, GPU resources or recognition
accuracy. Worker model/recipe identifiers are requested constants, not attestations.

Native extraction refuses an undeterminable page count. If Poppler's `pdfinfo` is
absent and the page tree is not readable in the raw file -- typically because a
modern producer stored it in a compressed object stream -- the capture is
refused with an explicit error rather than silently retaining only the first
page. Install Poppler or configure `LIXITY_OCR_WORKER` to ingest such a file.

Pass `--fallback` (or set `LIXITY_OCR_FALLBACK=1`) to permit native `pdftotext`
extraction if worker execution fails/times out or Tesseract extraction fails.
The result records a warning; review mixed/scanned pages for missing text.
Without explicit fallback, these failures reject the capture.

### Use local OCR without a worker service

Install Poppler, Tesseract and required language data on the server computer.
Select the backend in that service's environment and restart it:

```sh
export LIXITY_OCR_BACKEND=tesseract
export LIXITY_OCR_LANGUAGES=deu+eng
lixity research ocr-status --probe
```

Backends are `native`, `worker` or `tesseract`. When unset, a configured worker
wins, otherwise native Poppler is default. Explicit `worker_cmd`/`--worker-cmd`
wins over environment. Tesseract defaults to `eng`; requested languages must be
installed. Diagnostics report requested/available/missing data; nothing downloads
or starts automatically. Tesseract renders at 300 dpi with a bounded invocation
deadline; workers retain their 150 dpi protocol. Failures reject unless explicit
native fallback is allowed. A synthetic probe checks execution, not recognition.
New captures identify `tesseract-cli/1` or `poppler-native/1` and require storage
v4. Earlier cached provenance/bytes remain unchanged.

### Worker interface

Read [Unlimited-OCR integration and deployment boundaries](OCR_INTEGRATION.md)
before provisioning inference. Baidu's official entrypoints do not implement
this custom worker protocol; a separate adapter is required.

Set `LIXITY_OCR_WORKER` to one executable path or a command name on PATH. It is
invoked directly as `[worker, request_file]`, without shell parsing or embedded
arguments. Use an absolute path without `~` for portable service configuration.
`LIXITY_OCR_TIMEOUT` sets the worker subprocess deadline in seconds: an integer
from 1 to 3600, default 120. This is a total invocation deadline, not per page.
Set the variable in the service's environment and restart the server; exporting
it in another terminal does not update an existing process.

The temporary request JSON contains:

```json
{
  "model_snapshot": "<requested model snapshot>",
  "recipe_revision": "<requested recipe revision>",
  "pdf_path": "/absolute/path/to/input.pdf",
  "pages": [{"page_number": 1, "sha256": "<rendered PNG SHA-256>"}]
}
```

The [deployment reference](OCR_INTEGRATION.md) records the integration pins.
The worker provisions its own runtime/models; request identifiers do not attest
that an executable used those weights.
The request includes PDF access and page checksums, not image paths or image
bytes. A worker that needs raster images must obtain them from the local PDF.

Return JSON on stdout; send logs to stderr:

```json
{"blocks": [{"page_number": 1, "text": "Synthetic reading room note."}], "warnings": []}
```

Worker responses are validated before accepting a capture.
Every block needs a nonempty string `text` and an integer `page_number` from the
rendered request pages; at most 5,000 blocks are accepted. Optional `box` contains
four finite numbers. Optional `confidence` must be a finite number from 0 to 1;
omission or `null` means **unknown**, never an implicit score of 1.0. A supplied
score is worker-reported, not an independently calibrated accuracy estimate.

Every requested page must be covered by a block or listed in optional
`completed_pages`. Use that integer list for pages successfully inspected with
no readable text, such as a blank page; never use it to conceal a failed page.
For example, a two-page document with a blank second page may return:

```json
{"blocks": [{"page_number": 1, "text": "Synthetic note."}], "completed_pages": [2], "warnings": []}
```

Warnings, when supplied, must be a list of strings. Blocks are ordered by page
number while retaining their supplied order within each page; their trimmed text
is joined with blank lines. Coverage validates what the worker reports, not
whether it recognized every word. A completely textless document still cannot
be ingested as a searchable source.

A configured worker's nonzero exit or timeout fails the import by default;
explicit `--fallback` / `LIXITY_OCR_FALLBACK` can permit native text extraction
with a warning. Invalid block structure or missing reported page coverage still
fails closed. There is no silent native-text fallback. With no backend or worker configured, native
text-layer extraction remains available and can omit scanned pages; inspect mixed
PDFs for completeness. A successful native import is not an OCR-success claim.

For local scans, use the built-in Tesseract backend described above. Custom model
deployment belongs to a separately maintained adapter implementing this worker
protocol. The [adapter reference](OCR_INTEGRATION.md#historical-cpu-experiment)
records the retired CPU experiment.

### What is actually retained

`SourceVersion.blob` identifies original PDF bytes; `Extraction.text_blob` holds
extracted UTF-8. Passages cite exact character spans in that text. Page images,
boxes, confidence and runtime warnings are not retained as audited coordinate or
accuracy records, nor is there an attestation of which model ran.

`research-ingest-local/1` returns `warnings: list[str]` for committed, preview
and unchanged results. Successful local/Zotero batch items preserve them. Clean
or reused extraction returns `[]`; an unchanged response does not recover earlier
warnings. Save needed operational diagnostics separately and verify quotations
against the original scan. Core import is local; a configured worker's network
behavior belongs to its deployment's privacy boundary.

## Safe Markdown and offline diagram rendering

Dossier bodies support headings, emphasis, quotations, lists, code, tables,
callouts and a bounded subset of inline/display math. This is not a full
CommonMark or LaTeX implementation. Raw HTML stays escaped. The bundled Mermaid
Tiny renderer processes supported `mermaid` fences offline.
The library initializes when a diagram first becomes visible. Image/resource
syntax, click actions and configuration/style directives are disabled; unsupported
or invalid diagrams keep their inspectable source. Rendered SVGs share the local
PhotoSwipe zoom viewer with images. Both libraries run locally. Map tiles have
the separate network boundary above. For library versions and integration
details, see the [vendored media inventory](https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/src/lixity/ui/assets/vendor/README.md#research-media).

A small diagram uses a compact frame. Wide diagrams
keep their label size and scroll horizontally within the reader; focus the
viewport and use the arrow keys, or choose **Enlarge diagram**. The source remains
available below it. The renderer preserves the direction and relationships in
your Mermaid source; visual proximity does not establish evidence or causality.

## Limits

Research uses operation-specific `*-local/N` response envelopes and versioned
records/manifests, independently of the product version. It does not implement
the RFC's illustrative `research/1` bundle. Unknown fields/versions fail closed.
Check installed support with `lixity about --json` and entity contracts with
`lixity research schema`.

The [local data model](DATA_MODEL.md#schema-evolution-and-compatibility) maps
each write capability to its required record and manifest versions. Reading
alone keeps the format unchanged. Back up the complete store before opting in
to a higher format and use compatible readers and writers afterward.
Historical v3.0.1 supports through v6, v0.6.0 through v7, and v0.7.0/v0.7.1 through v8.
Clients without v9 support cannot open an archive after its first v9 media
capture. Physical manifest compression has a separate compatibility boundary:
see [manifest migration](#migrate-manifest-storage).
Rollback requires the complete pre-upgrade backup, never editing HEAD, schema
labels or provenance by hand. Source identity metadata cannot be edited in place;
refresh creates a new capture.

The 100,000-entry snapshot limit includes retained revisions. Status counts show
current logical records; the audit's `records` count includes their history.
Each accepted write retains a complete manifest of accepted revision entries,
so manifest storage can grow faster than the newly added record bytes. Unchanged
authored edits create no snapshot; batch operations reduce the number of complete
manifests compared with separate writes. Keep old manifests: backup verifies their
complete parent chain. The current live store compresses each complete manifest;
[explicit migration](#migrate-manifest-storage) converts older plaintext stores.
Delta manifests and pruning accepted history are not implemented.

Text inputs are at most 2 MiB and must be valid UTF-8 without NUL bytes.
PDF inputs are at most 50 MiB. Both routes allow at most 5,000 nonempty extracted
passages. Search uses literal Unicode words joined with AND; it is
not stemming, translation or semantic search. BM25 scores are ranks, not truth
probabilities. Language tags do not translate quotations. Empty or whitespace-only
queries fail validation. Queries with no searchable words return no matches.
Missing FTS5 support produces an error. For SQLite failures, the search error
reports the path and the SQLite cause. After resolving the cause, use
`research reindex` to rebuild the
disposable catalogue. A rebuild failure before replacement keeps the previously
published index; rebuilding does not modify canonical research records.
Source analysis emits `original_language_supplied` when source context names
an original language; that free-text field alone does not establish historical
language variety. This replaces the earlier experimental
`historical_language` limitation code.

Audits check retained records, hashes and citations, not factual accuracy,
permissions or historical completeness. A citation's `availability` indicates
whether its source is currently available or withdrawn; a purged passage no
longer resolves. The web panel displays those evidence states for linked
passages.
The [licensing rules](../LICENSING.md) still apply; imported sources keep
their own rights.

===============================================================================
## docs/METHODS.md

Source: https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/docs/METHODS.md

# Mathematical methods

> Version line: this documentation describes source **v0.9.3** on the pre-1.0 **0.x** line.
> Historical 1.x/3.x tags predate the numbering reset; a larger number does not mean a newer release.

Definitions, defaults and implementation limits of Lixity's measurements for
manuscript revision and exploratory linguistic text analysis. Start with the
[linguistic workflow](USAGE.md#linguistic-text-analysis) to preserve inputs,
settings and outputs for reproducible work.
Research context and known limitations live in
[`STABILITY.md`](STABILITY.md); command flags live in [`USAGE.md`](USAGE.md).

Review thresholds are configurable heuristics, not universal laws. Read their
active values from passport `meta`; formula constants and estimator conventions
are separate from author preferences.

The earlier 1.25 corrections changed measurements and derived results.
Passport schema 5 also changes the ordered-baseline diagnostics described below.
Regenerate chapter
metrics, style passports and reports before comparing outputs from before the
prose-scope, MTLD, robust-scale, segmentation, distribution and dimension
corrections. A source update alone does not refresh stored outputs.

## 1. Robust house-style baseline

The reference population is the supplied manuscript's measurable chapters.
Retained research sources, including travel accounts and monographs, are not
added to that population. Source analysis uses the same engine on one archived
source version and labels its interpretation `source_internal`; an explicit
source–manuscript comparison produces a separate report, not a new baseline.

### Language and presentation boundary

Language selection changes tokenization, linguistic feature extraction and
the readability model. It does not translate or alter the definitions of
median/MAD, FDR correction or eigendecomposition. JSON numbers remain numeric;
locale-specific decimal separators are applied only when rendering reports.
See [LOCALIZATION.md](LOCALIZATION.md) for supported profiles and limitations.

Token, syllable, dialogue and sentence measures share the supported prose scope:
body paragraphs, list items and blockquote paragraphs with `>` delimiters
removed. YAML front matter, code, headings, comments and footnote definitions
are omitted; inline emphasis and footnote anchors are stripped. Sentence
boundaries never cross a blank line: each semantic block is split on its own,
and a block without terminal punctuation stays one fragment unit. This bounded
Markdown policy is not a complete CommonMark parser. Visible prose beneath a
leading document title (`# …`) before the first chapter contributes to global
metrics but not chapter-only reports.
When no document title precedes the chapters, opening prose is measured as
part of the opening chapter. Sentence punctuation and soft wraps help
distinguish prose from a bare title line, which retains its title role.
Paragraph profiles intentionally cover body paragraphs and list items only,
retaining their source line anchors; they omit blockquotes.

The global function-word share is `100 × matching function-word tokens / all
counted tokens` in that same corpus prose scope. Its overview tile uses the
corpus measurement, rather than an unweighted mean of paragraph percentages.
The `CorpusMetrics.function_word_pct` field is `null` when the language profile
has no function-word list, the corpus has no counted tokens, or an older payload
omits the field. The UI reports the missing measurement explicitly.

Configured `word_regex` flags are respected across analysis surfaces; cue
patterns retain their separate case-insensitive contract. The cue pattern
selects the hits and the word pattern supplies the density denominator. A word
pattern may have zero capturing groups (each whole match is a token) or one (its capture
is the token). Multiple capturing groups are rejected with a configuration
error; use noncapturing `(?:...)` groups for additional regex structure.
English and German
default word patterns include Unicode accented letters. LF and CRLF share
semantic paragraph boundaries. Short-paragraph counting uses paragraph
whitespace words and the inclusive configured threshold, including eight-word
paragraphs. Legacy whitespace counts remain distinct from regex token counts.

**Since v0.7.6:** the shared Markdown counting projection uses Unicode NFC for
token, vocabulary, cue and syllable measurements. Configured word/cue patterns
operate on that canonical counting text; their flags are unchanged. Document
boundary patterns and appendix markers still address the original source. Manuscript
bytes, displayed quotations, line anchors and source hashes are not normalized.
Appendix examples inside fenced code or within a longer HTML comment leave
the following prose in scope. A whole comment configured as the marker can
still end the analysis.
Literal evidence maps complete canonical clusters back to original codepoint
ranges; ambiguous inner-cluster cuts retain counts with unavailable mapping.
Legacy raw/clean character counts still describe original codepoints, not
grapheme clusters. This is canonical equivalence, not general linguistic word
segmentation; see [Unicode UAX #29](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr29/).

Sentence-length measurements apply the word pattern to each recognized sentence
and average the resulting nonempty lengths. Paragraph totals apply the pattern
to the paragraph. Boundary-sensitive custom patterns can yield different totals
at those scopes.

The global UI word count uses the corpus token measurement, matching its sentence
and ASL values. Paragraph/chapter profile views remain narrower: pre-chapter
prose and blockquotes can contribute to corpus counts without paragraph profiles.
The two scope explanations are separate; a missing profile is not missing prose.

v0.7.2 corrects internal straight (`'`) and curly (`’`) apostrophes in the French,
Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and Dutch default word patterns. These orthographic
tokens follow the existing profile convention, not grammatical clitic analysis.
First-person starter matching (`first_person_start_rate` in `analyzer.py`)
extracts each sentence's first `word_regex` token match (lowercased; sentences
without a word-token match are excluded from the denominator), checks both the
full token and its pre-apostrophe stem (`first.replace("’", "'").split("'", 1)[0]`,
e.g. `j'aime -> j`, `i'm -> i`) against the language profile's
`first_person_starters`, and reports `100 × matching_sentences / token_bearing_sentences`
(`0.0` when no sentence contains a word token, or for `generic` which has an
empty starter set). Sentence-start Shannon entropy (`start_entropy`) retains the
exact unstemmed lowercased starter frequencies over the same denominator.
Recompute affected token counts, derived measurements and first-person start
rates before comparing older outputs.

Chapter labels remain available for navigation; changing a title does not
change its prose readability. For even sentence counts, `median_sl_exact`
averages the two middle lengths. The older integer `median_sl` retains its upper
middle value for JSON compatibility; reports use the exact median.

Corpus `dialog_words` and chapter dialogue counts use the configured
`word_regex`, as do their denominators (`tokens` and chapter `words`). Thus
`dialog_ratio` and chapter `dialog_pct` count the same token unit inside and
outside detected quotations. The legacy whitespace count `clean_words` is
unchanged and is not the dialogue-ratio denominator. Recompute older dialogue
reports and dependent style results before comparing across this correction.

The manuscript reader shows the recognized words and the paragraph word count.
A paragraph containing just one marked reply can contribute all of its words.
Chapter bars use the chapter's full analyzed word count to show how much of its
prose falls within recognized marks.

### Perception/filter word cues

Density features (`filter_density`, modal, passive, nominalisation) are counts
over the whole prose scope including detected quotations: a perception verb in
direct speech contributes like one in the narrating voice. The reports do not
attribute speakers. Treat a high density together with the chapter's
`dialog_pct` — a value carried by dialogue is characterisation, not narration.
A narrative-only variant of these densities is a documented candidate for a
future schema, not part of the current contract.

Since v0.7.2 the German cue list includes the indicative present and simple-past
forms of **hören** and **riechen**, alongside the existing listed forms. Their
spellings follow Duden's [hören](https://www.duden.de/konjugation/hoeren) and
[riechen](https://www.duden.de/konjugation/riechen) tables. This is a bounded lexical
extension, not a lemmatizer or a test of narrative distance. For example, a room
that *riecht nach Farbe* contributes a match even without a perceiving narrator;
a somatic description without a listed verb can contribute none. Compounds,
all tenses, subjunctives and participles are not exhaustively covered; ambiguous
*gehört* is not added as a standalone cue. Project `filter_verbs_regex` replaces
the list, including an explicitly empty pattern. Zero means no listed matches,
not an ideal style. Regenerate German filter densities and dependent comparisons
before comparing reports across this change.

### Dimension cutoffs and robust baselines

The 3D dashboard displays up to three derived dimension scores. A point is
flagged when a completed dimension score reaches the configured absolute
cutoff on any displayed axis. All feature contributions must be summed before
testing that cutoff: intermediate partial sums are not dimension scores.
The visual boundary is therefore a box of per-axis cutoffs, not a sphere or
a joint confidence region. Camera rotation and zoom do not change scores.

Per feature $f$ over $n$ measurable chapters with values $x_1,\dots,x_n$:
